body.translated_text: <s>Bhāvamiśra</s>: <s>Bhāvaprakāśaḥ</s>

children.translated_text: <s>Bhāvaprakāśa</s>, <s>Vargaprakaraṇa</s> (Chapter on Classification), <s>Harītakyādivarga</s> (Section on Harītakī and Others)

children.text: dakṣaṃ prajāpatiṃ vastham aśvinau vākyam ūcatuḥ /
children.translated_text: The two <s>Aśvins</s> addressed <s>Dakṣa</s> <s>Prajāpati</s> with these words:

children.text: kuto harītakī jātā tasyāstu kati jātayaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: From where was <s>Harītakī</s> born, and how many varieties does it have? // 1

children.text: rasāḥ kati samākhyātāḥ kati coparasāḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: How many <s>rasas</s> (tastes) are described, and how many <s>uparasas</s> (secondary tastes) are known?

children.text: nāmāni kati coktāni kiṃvā tāsāṃ ca lakṣaṇam // 2
children.translated_text: How many names have been stated, and what are their characteristics? // 2

children.text: ke ca varṇā guṇāḥ ke ca kā ca kutra prayujyate /
children.translated_text: What are the colors, what are the properties, and where is each one used?

children.text: kena dravyeṇa saṃyuktā kāṃś ca rogān vyapohati // 3
children.translated_text: Combined with what substance does it remove which diseases? // 3
O Blessed One, please speak as these questions have been asked.
Having heard the words of the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s> spoke these words: // 4
A drop fell upon the earth when <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) was drinking <s>amṛta</s> (nectar),
From that divine [drop] arose <s>Harītakī</s> of seven varieties. // 5
<s>Harītakī</s>, <s>Abhayā</s>, <s>Pathyā</s>, <s>Kāyasthā</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s>,
<s>Haimavatī</s>, <s>Avyathā</s>, and also <s>Cetakī</s>, <s>Śreyasī</s>, <s>Śivā</s>, // 6

body.text: vayaḥsthā vijayā cāpi jīvantī rohiṇīti ca // 7
body.translated_text: <s>Vayaḥsthā</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, and also <s>Jīvantī</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s> — thus. // 7

children.translated_text: <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, and also <s>Pūtanā</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s>, <s>Abhayā</s>,

children.text: jīvantī cetakī ceti pathyāyāḥ sapta jātayaḥ // 8
children.translated_text: <s>Jīvantī</s> and <s>Cetakī</s> — these are the seven varieties of <s>Pathyā</s>. // 8

children.text: vindhyādrau vijayā himācalabhavā syāccetakī pūtanā sindhau syādatha rohiṇī nigaditā jātā pratiṣṭhānake /
children.translated_text: <s>Vijayā</s> grows in the <s>Vindhya</s> mountains; <s>Cetakī</s> is born in the <s>Himālaya</s>; <s>Pūtanā</s> grows in <s>Sindhu</s>; <s>Rohiṇī</s> is said to be born in <s>Pratiṣṭhānaka</s>;

children.text: campāyām amṛtābhayā ca janitā deśe surāṣṭrāhvaye jīvantīti harītakī nigaditā sapta prabhedā budhaiḥ // 9
children.translated_text: <s>Amṛtā</s> and <s>Abhayā</s> are produced in <s>Campā</s>; in the land called <s>Surāṣṭra</s>, <s>Jīvantī</s> — thus <s>Harītakī</s> is described by the wise as having seven varieties. // 9

children.text: alābuvṛttā vijayā vṛttā sā rohiṇī smṛtā /
children.translated_text: <s>Vijayā</s> is gourd-shaped; <s>Rohiṇī</s> is known to be round;
<s>Pūtanā</s> has a large stone; <s>Amṛtā</s> is described as fleshy and fine. // 10
<s>Abhayā</s> is said to have five ridges; <s>Jīvantī</s> is golden in color;
<s>Cetakī</s> is known to have three ridges — this is the appearance of the seven. // 11
<s>Vijayā</s> is [used] in all diseases; <s>Rohiṇī</s> heals wounds;
<s>Pūtanā</s> should be used for poultices; <s>Amṛtā</s> is beneficial for purification purposes. // 12
<s>Abhayā</s> is excellent for eye diseases; <s>Jīvantī</s> destroys all diseases;
<s>Cetakī</s> is excellent for use in powder form — one should employ [each] as appropriate. // 13

children.text: cetakī dvividhā proktā śvetā kṛṣṇā ca varṇataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Cetakī</s> is said to be of two kinds: white and black in color;

children.text: ṣaḍaṅgulāyatā śuklā kṛṣṇā tv ekāṅgulā smṛtā // 14
children.translated_text: The white one is six <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-widths) long; the black one is known to be one <s>aṅgula</s>. // 14
One [type] purges merely by tasting; another by smelling;
Another by touch, another by sight — thus <s>Śivā</s> (Harītakī) purges in four ways. // 15
Those persons who approach the shade of a <s>Cetakī</s> tree,
They are purged at that very moment — animals, birds, deer, and others. // 16

children.text: cetakī tu dhṛtā haste yāvattiṣṭhati dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: As long as <s>Cetakī</s> is held in the hand of a person,
For that long one is purged by its powerful effects — there is no doubt in this. // 17
For kings, for the delicate, for the emaciated, and for those averse to medicine,
<s>Cetakī</s> is supremely excellent — beneficial and a comfortable purgative. // 18

children.text: saptānām api jātīnāṃ pradhānā vijayā smṛtā /
children.translated_text: Among all seven varieties, <s>Vijayā</s> is considered the chief;
Easy to use, readily available, it is praised for all diseases. // 19
<s>Harītakī</s> has five <s>rasas</s> (tastes) except salty; it is predominantly astringent;
It is dry, hot, appetizing, intellect-promoting, sweet in <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect), and a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative). // 20
It is beneficial for the eyes, light, life-promoting, nourishing, and laxative;

It destroys <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), <s>kāsa</s> (cough), <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders), <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), <s>śotha</s> (edema), <s>udara</s> (abdominal diseases), and <s>krimī</s> (worms). // 21
It cures <s>vaisvarya</s> (hoarseness), <s>grahaṇīroga</s> (malabsorption), constipation, and <s>viṣamajvara</s> (intermittent fever),
<s>Gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>ādhmāna</s> (flatulence), <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (thirst), <s>chardi</s> (vomiting), <s>hikkā</s> (hiccup), <s>kaṇḍū</s> (itching), and heart diseases. // 22
It [cures] <s>kāmalā</s> (jaundice), <s>śūla</s> (colic), <s>ānāha</s> (distension), diseases of the <s>plīhā</s> (spleen) and <s>yakṛt</s> (liver),

children.text: aśmarīṃ mūtrakṛcchraṃ ca mūtrāghātaṃ ca nāśayet // 23
children.translated_text: It destroys <s>aśmarī</s> (urinary stones), <s>mūtrakṛcchra</s> (dysuria), and <s>mūtrāghāta</s> (urinary obstruction). // 23
Due to its sweet, bitter, and astringent tastes, it alleviates <s>pitta</s>; it removes <s>kapha</s>;
Due to its pungent, bitter, and astringent tastes [it alleviates kapha], and due to its sour taste, <s>Śivā</s> removes <s>vāta</s>. // 24

body.translated_text: [One may ask:] Since it is pungent and sour, it should aggravate <s>pitta</s>, and since it alleviates <s>vāta</s> [through sourness], how can <s>Śivā</s> be [truly beneficial]? // 25

children.translated_text: Its power to destroy all <s>doṣas</s> is established through <s>prabhāva</s> (inherent potency); this is being explained —
Through reasoning, for the instruction of students; nothing new is being created now. // 26
Different actions [can be seen] despite similar properties, [and this] is observed due to differences in substrate;
Therefore one should not object, as in the case of <s>Dhātrī</s> (āmalaka) and <s>Lakuca</s> (breadfruit). // 27
In the kernel of <s>Pathyā</s> (Harītakī) the sweet taste resides; in the flesh, the sour taste is established;

children.text: vṛnte tiktas tvaci kaṭur asthisthas tuvaro rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the stalk it is bitter, in the bark it is pungent, and in the seed the astringent taste [is found].

children.text: snigdhā ghanā vṛttā gurvī kṣiptā ca yāmbhasi /
children.translated_text: That which is unctuous, dense, round, heavy, and when thrown in water
sinks — that is praised and said to be exceedingly beneficial. // 28
Possessing nine and more qualities, and also weighing two <s>karṣas</s> in a single fruit —
Where both these [qualities] are found in a <s>Harītakī</s> fruit, that is said to be the best. // 29
When chewed, it increases digestive fire; when ground [into paste], it purifies waste;

children.text: svinnā saṃgrāhiṇī pathyā bhṛṣṭā proktā tridoṣanut // 30
children.translated_text: When steamed, <s>Pathyā</s> is astringent; when roasted, it is said to cure all three <s>doṣas</s>. // 30
It opens the faculties of intellect, strength, and senses; it uproots <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>;
It loosens urine, feces, and waste — such is <s>Harītakī</s> when taken with food. // 31
The <s>doṣas</s> arising from food and drink, born of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> —
<s>Harītakī</s> quickly removes them when taken after eating. // 32

children.text: lavaṇena kaphaṃ hanti pittaṃ hanti saśarkarā /
children.translated_text: With salt, it destroys <s>kapha</s>; with sugar, it destroys <s>pitta</s>;
With <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee), it [cures] diseases born of <s>vāta</s>; with <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery), it [cures] all diseases. // 33
With <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), sugar, <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger), <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper), honey, and <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) respectively,
<s>Abhayā</s> should be consumed in the rainy and subsequent seasons by one seeking <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative) benefits. // 34

children.text: adhvātikhinno balavarjitaś ca rūkṣaḥ kṛśo laṅghanakarśitaśca /
children.translated_text: One who is exhausted from long travel, lacking strength, dry, emaciated, weakened by fasting,

children.text: pittādhiko garbhavatī ca nārī vimuktaraktastvabhayāṃ na khādet // 35
children.translated_text: One with excess <s>pitta</s>, a pregnant woman, or one who has just been bled — these should not eat <s>Abhayā</s>. // 35
<s>Vibhītaka</s> is of all three genders; it is [also called] <s>Akṣa</s> and <s>Karṣaphala</s>;
[Also known as] <s>Kalidruma</s>, <s>Bhūtavāsa</s>, and <s>Kaliyugālaya</s>. // 36
<s>Vibhītaka</s> is sweet in <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect), astringent, and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>;
It is hot in potency, cool to touch, laxative, and destroys <s>kāsa</s> (cough). // 37
It is dry, beneficial for the eyes, good for hair, and destroys worms and hoarseness.
The kernel of <s>Vibhītaka</s> alleviates thirst, vomiting, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>; it is light;
It is astringent and intoxicating; and the kernel of <s>Dhātrī</s> (āmalaka) has the same properties. // 38

body.translated_text: Among the three [fruits], it is called <s>Āmalaka</s>; [also known as] <s>Dhātrī</s>, <s>Tiṣyaphala</s>, and <s>Amṛtā</s>. // 39

children.translated_text: The fruit of <s>Dhātrī</s> (āmalaka) is equal to <s>Harītakī</s>, but especially:
It destroys <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders) and <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders); it is supremely aphrodisiac and a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative). // 40
It alleviates <s>vāta</s> through its sourness, <s>pitta</s> through its sweetness and coolness,
And <s>kapha</s> through its dryness and astringency — thus the fruit of <s>Dhātrī</s> conquers all three <s>doṣas</s>. // 41

children.text: yasya yasya phalasyeha vīryaṃ bhavati yādṛśam /
children.translated_text: Whatever the potency of a given fruit may be,
By that same potency one should prescribe its kernel as well. // 42
With equal [parts of] the fruits of <s>Pathyā</s> (Harītakī), <s>Vibhītaka</s>, and <s>Dhātrī</s>, there is <s>Triphalā</s>;

children.text: phalatrikaṃ ca triphalā sā varā ca prakīrtitā // 43
children.translated_text: The three-fruit [combination] is <s>Triphalā</s>, and it is also called <s>Varā</s>. // 43
<s>Triphalā</s> destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, removes <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders) and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), and is laxative;
It is beneficial for the eyes, appetizing, taste-promoting, and destroys <s>viṣamajvara</s> (intermittent fever). // 44

children.text: śuṇṭhī viśvā ca viśvaṃ ca nāgaraṃ viśvabheṣajam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger) [is also known as] <s>Viśvā</s>, <s>Viśvam</s>, <s>Nāgara</s>, <s>Viśvabheṣaja</s> (universal medicine),
<s>Ūṣaṇa</s>, <s>Kaṭubhadra</s>, <s>Śṛṅgavera</s>, and <s>Mahauṣadha</s> (great medicine). // 45
<s>Śuṇṭhī</s> promotes taste, removes <s>āma</s> (undigested toxins) and <s>vāta</s>, is digestive, pungent, and light;
It is unctuous, hot, sweet in <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect), and removes <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, and constipation. // 46
It is aphrodisiac, voice-improving, and destroys <s>vami</s> (vomiting), <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), <s>śūla</s> (colic), <s>kāsa</s> (cough), and heart diseases;
It destroys <s>ślīpada</s> (elephantiasis), <s>śotha</s> (edema), <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), <s>ānāha</s> (distension), <s>udara</s> (abdominal diseases), and <s>vāta</s> disorders. // 47
Because it predominantly possesses fiery qualities and dries up the water element,

children.text: saṃgṛhṇāti malaṃ tattu grāhi śuṇṭhyādayo yathā // 48
children.translated_text: It absorbs waste matter — hence it is <s>grāhī</s> (absorbent/binding), as in the case of <s>Śuṇṭhī</s> and others. // 48

children.text: vibandhabhedinī yā tu sā kathaṃ grāhiṇī bhavet /
children.translated_text: How can that which breaks constipation be absorbent/binding?
Its potency is in breaking obstruction, not in causing fecal discharge. // 49
<s>Ārdraka</s> (fresh ginger) is [also called] <s>Śṛṅgavera</s>, <s>Kaṭubhadra</s>, and <s>Ārdrikā</s>.

children.text: ārdrikā bhedinī gurvī tīkṣṇoṣṇā dīpanī matā // 50
children.translated_text: <s>Ārdrikā</s> is laxative, heavy, sharp, hot, and appetizing. // 50
It is pungent, sweet in <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect), dry, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
All the properties described for <s>Śuṇṭhī</s> are also present in <s>Ārdraka</s>. // 51
Before meals, it is always beneficial to eat [fresh ginger] with salt —
It kindles the digestive fire, promotes taste, and cleanses the tongue and throat. // 52
In <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), edema, dysentery, <s>mūtrakṛcchra</s> (dysuria), <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), wounds, fever,
Burning sensation, and during the hot season and autumn — <s>Ārdraka</s> is not recommended. // 53

children.text: pippalī māgadhī kṛṣṇā vaidehī capalā kaṇā /
children.translated_text: <s>Pippalī</s> (long pepper) [is also known as] <s>Māgadhī</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Capalā</s>, <s>Kaṇā</s>,
<s>Upakulyā</s>, <s>Ūṣaṇā</s>, <s>Śauṇḍī</s>, <s>Kolā</s>, and <s>Tīkṣṇataṇḍulā</s>. // 54
<s>Pippalī</s> is appetizing, aphrodisiac, sweet in <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect), a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative),
Not hot, pungent, unctuous, light, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣma</s> (kapha). // 55
<s>Pippalī</s> is purgative and destroys <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), <s>kāsa</s> (cough), <s>udara</s> (abdominal diseases), and <s>jvara</s> (fever),

<s>Kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders), <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), <s>plīha</s> (splenic disorders), <s>śūla</s> (colic), <s>āma</s> (undigested toxins), and <s>vāta</s> disorders. // 56

children.text: ārdrā kaphapradā snigdhā śītalā madhurā guruḥ /
children.translated_text: When fresh, it increases <s>kapha</s>, is unctuous, cooling, sweet, and heavy;
It pacifies <s>pitta</s>; but when dry, it aggravates <s>pitta</s>. // 57
<s>Pippalī</s> combined with honey destroys <s>medas</s> (fat) and <s>kapha</s>;
It removes <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), <s>kāsa</s> (cough), and <s>jvara</s> (fever); it is aphrodisiac, intellect-promoting, and increases digestive fire. // 58
In chronic fever and digestive weakness, <s>guḍapippalī</s> (jaggery with long pepper) is recommended;
It cures <s>kāsa</s> (cough), indigestion, anorexia, <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), heart diseases, <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), and worm diseases.
The <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) should be twice the quantity of <s>pippalī</s> powder — this is the opinion of physicians. // 59

body.translated_text: <s>Marica</s> (black pepper) [is also known as] <s>Vellaja</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Ūṣaṇa</s>, and <s>Dharmapattana</s>. // 60

children.translated_text: <s>Marica</s> is pungent, sharp, appetizing, and conquers <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>;
It is hot, aggravates <s>pitta</s>, is dry, and removes <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), <s>śūla</s> (colic), and <s>krimī</s> (worms). // 61

children.text: tadārdraṃ madhuraṃ pāke nātyuṣṇaṃ kaṭukaṃ guru /
children.translated_text: When fresh, it is sweet in <s>vipāka</s>, not very hot, pungent, and heavy;
It has slightly sharp properties, increases <s>śleṣma</s> (kapha secretion), and does not aggravate <s>pitta</s>. // 62
<s>Viśvā</s> (dry ginger), <s>Upakulyā</s> (long pepper), and <s>Marica</s> (black pepper) — these three are called <s>Trikaṭu</s>;

children.text: kaṭutrikaṃ tu trikaṭu tryūṣaṇaṃ vyoṣa ucyate // 63
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṭutrika</s> is <s>Trikaṭu</s>, [also called] <s>Tryūṣaṇa</s> and <s>Vyoṣa</s>. // 63
<s>Tryūṣaṇa</s> is appetizing and destroys <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), <s>kāsa</s> (cough), and skin diseases,
<s>Gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders), <s>kapha</s>, <s>sthaulya</s> (obesity), <s>medas</s> (fat), <s>ślīpada</s> (elephantiasis), and <s>pīnasa</s> (rhinitis). // 64
<s>Granthika</s> [is another name for] <s>Pippalīmūla</s> (root of long pepper); [also called] <s>Ūṣaṇa</s> and <s>Caṭakāśiras</s>.
<s>Pippalīmūla</s> is appetizing, pungent, hot, digestive, and light. // 65
It is dry, aggravates <s>pitta</s>, is laxative, and removes <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, and <s>udara</s> (abdominal diseases);
It destroys <s>ānāha</s> (distension), <s>plīha</s> (splenic disorders), <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>krimī</s> (worms), <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), and <s>kṣaya</s> (wasting). // 66
<s>Tryūṣaṇa</s> with <s>pippalīmūla</s> (long pepper root) is called <s>Caturūṣaṇa</s> (four pungents);
The properties of <s>Vyoṣa</s> (Trikaṭu) are stated [for it], but <s>Caturūṣaṇa</s> has additional [benefits]. // 67

children.text: bhaveccavyaṃ tu cavikā kathitā sā tathoṣaṇā /
children.translated_text: <s>Cavya</s> is also called <s>Cavikā</s> and <s>Ūṣaṇā</s>;
<s>Cavya</s> has properties similar to <s>pippalīmūla</s>, and especially removes <s>gudaja</s> (rectal) [disorders]. // 68
The fruit of <s>Cavikā</s> is called <s>Gajapippalī</s> by the wise;
[Also known as] <s>Kapivallī</s>, <s>Kolavallī</s>, <s>Śreyasī</s>, and <s>Vaśira</s>. // 69
<s>Gajakṛṣṇā</s> (Gajapippalī) is pungent, removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣma</s> (kapha), and increases digestive fire;
It is hot and destroys <s>atīsāra</s> (diarrhea), <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), throat diseases, and <s>krimī</s> (worms). // 70
<s>Citraka</s> (leadwort) is [also known as] <s>Anala</s>, <s>Pīṭha</s>, <s>Vyāla</s>, and <s>Ūṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: citrakaḥ kaṭukaḥ pāke vahnikṛt pācano laghuḥ // 71
children.translated_text: <s>Citraka</s> is pungent in <s>vipāka</s>, fire-kindling, digestive, and light. // 71
It is dry, hot, and removes <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), <s>śotha</s> (edema), <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), <s>krimī</s> (worms), and <s>kāsa</s> (cough);
It removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣma</s> (kapha), is absorbent, destroys <s>vāta</s>, and alleviates <s>śleṣma</s> and <s>pitta</s>. // 72
<s>Pippalī</s>, <s>Pippalīmūla</s>, <s>Cavya</s>, <s>Citraka</s>, and <s>Nāgara</s> (dry ginger) —
A <s>kola</s>-sized [portion] of these five is called <s>Pañcakola</s> (five pungents). // 73
<s>Pañcakola</s> is pungent in taste and <s>vipāka</s>, promotes taste,
Is sharp, hot, digestive, the best appetizer, and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>;

It destroys <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>plīha</s> (splenic disorders), <s>udara</s> (abdominal diseases), <s>ānāha</s> (distension), and <s>śūla</s> (colic), [but] aggravates <s>pitta</s>. // 74
<s>Pañcakola</s> with <s>Marica</s> (black pepper) is called <s>Ṣaḍūṣaṇa</s> (six pungents);
It has the properties of <s>Pañcakola</s>, is dry, hot, and removes poison. // 75

body.translated_text: <s>Yavānī</s> [is also known as] <s>Ugragandhā</s>, <s>Brahmadarbhā</s>, and <s>Ajamodikā</s>. // 76

children.text: saivoktā dīpyakā dīpyā tathā syād yavasāhvayā /
children.translated_text: It is also called <s>Dīpyakā</s>, <s>Dīpyā</s>, and <s>Yavasāhvayā</s>.

children.text: yavānī pācanī rucyā tīkṣṇoṣṇā kaṭukā laghuḥ // 77
children.translated_text: <s>Yavānī</s> is digestive, taste-promoting, sharp, hot, pungent, and light. // 77

children.text: dīpanī ca tathā tiktā pittalā śukraśūlahṛt /
children.translated_text: It is appetizing and also bitter, aggravates <s>pitta</s>, and removes <s>śukra</s> (seminal) and <s>śūla</s> (colic) [disorders];

It removes <s>vāta</s>, <s>śleṣma</s> (kapha), <s>udara</s> (abdominal diseases), <s>ānāha</s> (distension), <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>plīha</s> (splenic disorders), and <s>krimī</s> (worms). // 78

children.text: ajamodā kharāśvā ca māyūrī dīpyakas tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Ajamodā</s> [is also known as] <s>Kharāśvā</s>, <s>Māyūrī</s>, <s>Dīpyaka</s>,
And also <s>Brahmakuśā</s>, <s>Kāravī</s>, and <s>Locamastakā</s>. // 79
<s>Ajamodā</s> is pungent, sharp, appetizing, and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>;

children.text: uṣṇā vidāhinī hṛdyā vṛṣyā balakarī laghuḥ /
children.translated_text: It is hot, carminative, pleasant, aphrodisiac, strength-giving, and light;
It removes eye diseases, <s>krimī</s> (worms), <s>chardi</s> (vomiting), <s>hikkā</s> (hiccup), and bladder pain. // 80
<s>Pārasīka Yavānī</s> (Persian ajwain) has properties similar to <s>Yavānī</s>;
Especially, it is digestive, taste-promoting, absorbent, intoxicating, and heavy. // 81

body.translated_text: <s>Jīraka</s> (cumin) [is also known as] <s>Jaraṇa</s>, <s>Ajājī</s>; <s>Kaṇā</s> is <s>Dīrghajīraka</s> (long cumin). // 82

children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇajīra</s> (black cumin) [is also known as] <s>Sugandha</s> and <s>Udgāraśodhana</s>;
<s>Kālājājī</s> is [also called] <s>Suṣavī</s>, <s>Kālikā</s>, and <s>Upakālikā</s>. // 83
<s>Pṛthvīkā</s>, <s>Kāravī</s>, <s>Pṛthvī</s>, <s>Pṛthukṛṣṇā</s>, and <s>Upakuñcikā</s>,

children.text: upakuñcī ca kuñcī ca bṛhajjīraka ityapi // 84
children.translated_text: <s>Upakuñcī</s>, <s>Kuñcī</s>, and <s>Bṛhajjīraka</s> — [these are also names]. // 84
The three types of <s>Jīraka</s> are dry, pungent, hot, appetizing, and light;
They are absorbent, aggravate <s>pitta</s>, promote intellect, and purify the womb. // 85

children.text: jvaraghnaṃ pāvanaṃ vṛṣyaṃ balyaṃ rucyaṃ kaphāpaham /
children.translated_text: They destroy fever, are purifying, aphrodisiac, strengthening, taste-promoting, and remove <s>kapha</s>;
They are beneficial for the eyes and remove <s>vāta</s>, <s>ādhmāna</s> (flatulence), <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>chardi</s> (vomiting), and <s>atīsāra</s> (diarrhea). // 86

children.text: dhānyakaṃ dhānakaṃ dhānyaṃ dhānā dhāneyakaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Dhānyaka</s> (coriander) [is also known as] <s>Dhānaka</s>, <s>Dhānya</s>, <s>Dhānā</s>, <s>Dhāneyaka</s>,
<s>Kunaṭī</s>, <s>Dhenukā</s>, <s>Chattrā</s>, <s>Kustumburu</s>, and <s>Vitunnaka</s>. // 87
<s>Dhānyaka</s> is astringent, unctuous, not aphrodisiac, diuretic, and light;

children.text: tiktaṃ kaṭūṣṇavīryaṃ ca dīpanaṃ pācanaṃ smṛtam // 88
children.translated_text: It is bitter, pungent, hot in potency, appetizing, and digestive. // 88
It destroys fever, promotes taste, is absorbent, sweet in <s>vipāka</s>, and conquers all three <s>doṣas</s>;
It removes thirst, burning sensation, vomiting, <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), <s>kāsa</s> (cough), emaciation, and worms.
When fresh, it has the same properties [and is] sweet, but especially destroys <s>pitta</s>. // 89

children.text: śatapuṣpā śatāhvā ca madhurā kāravī misiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śatapuṣpā</s> (dill) [is also known as] <s>Śatāhvā</s>, <s>Madhurā</s>, <s>Kāravī</s>, and <s>Misi</s>;
[Also] <s>Atilambī</s>, <s>Sitacchattrā</s>, and <s>Saṃhitachattrikā</s>. // 90
<s>Chattrā</s>, <s>Śāleyaśālīna</s>, <s>Miśreyā</s>, <s>Madhurā</s>, and <s>Misi</s> [are names of fennel].
<s>Śatapuṣpā</s> is light, sharp, aggravates <s>pitta</s>, is appetizing, and pungent. // 91
It is hot and removes <s>jvara</s> (fever), <s>vāta</s>, <s>śleṣma</s> (kapha), wounds, <s>śūla</s> (colic), and eye diseases.
<s>Miśreyā</s> (fennel) has similar properties, but especially removes <s>yoniśūla</s> (uterine pain). // 92
It removes digestive weakness, is pleasant, and removes constipated feces, <s>krimī</s> (worms), and <s>śukra</s> (seminal disorders);
It is dry, hot, digestive, and removes <s>kāsa</s> (cough), <s>vami</s> (vomiting), <s>śleṣma</s> (kapha), and <s>vāta</s>. // 93
<s>Methikā</s> (fenugreek) [is also called] <s>methinī</s>, <s>methī</s>, <s>dīpanī</s> (digestive stimulant), and <s>bahupattrikā</s> (many-leaved);
<s>Bodhinī</s>, <s>bahubījā</s> (many-seeded), and <s>jyotirgandhaphalā</s> (luminous-fragrant-fruited). //94//

children.text: vallarī cakrikā manthā miśrapuṣpā ca kairavī /
children.translated_text: [It is also called] <s>vallarī</s>, <s>cakrikā</s>, <s>manthā</s>, <s>miśrapuṣpā</s> (mixed-flowered), and <s>kairavī</s>;
<s>Kuñcikā</s>, <s>bahuparṇī</s> (many-leaved), <s>pītabījā</s> (yellow-seeded), and <s>municchadā</s>. //95//
<s>Methikā</s> (fenugreek) alleviates <s>vāta</s> (wind), destroys <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), and eliminates <s>jvara</s> (fever);

children.text: tataḥ svalpaguṇā vanyā vājināṃ sā tu pūjitā // 96
children.translated_text: The wild variety has slightly lesser qualities; it is esteemed for horses. //96//
<s>Candrikā</s>, <s>carmahantrī</s> (skin-healer), and <s>paśumehanakārikā</s> (causing urination in animals);
<s>Nandinī</s>, <s>kāravī</s>, <s>bhadrā</s>, <s>vāsapuṣpā</s>, and <s>suvāsarā</s>. //97//
<s>Candraśūra</s> (garden cress) is beneficial for those suffering from hiccups, <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), and <s>atisāra</s> (diarrhea);
It counteracts blood and <s>vāta</s> diseases, and promotes strength and nourishment. //98//
<s>Methikā</s>, <s>candraśūra</s>, <s>kālājājī</s> (black cumin), and <s>yavānikā</s> (bishop's weed) —
These four together are known as <s>caturbīja</s> (the four seeds). //99//
The powder of that [<s>caturbīja</s>], consumed regularly, destroys diseases of <s>vāta</s> (wind),
Indigestion, colic, flatulence, pain in the sides, and pain in the loins. //100//

body.translated_text: <s>Sahasravedhi</s>, <s>jatuka</s>, <s>vāhlīka</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), and <s>rāmaṭha</s>. //101//

children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida) is hot, digestive, appetizing, pungent, and removes <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>balāsa</s> (phlegmatic disorders);
It destroys colic, abdominal tumors, abdominal enlargement, flatulence, and worms, and increases <s>pitta</s> (bile). //102//
<s>Vacā</s> (sweet flag) [is also called] <s>ugragandhā</s> (strong-smelling), <s>ṣaḍgranthā</s> (six-knotted), <s>golomī</s>, and <s>śataparvikā</s> (hundred-jointed);

children.text: kṣudrapattrī ca maṅgalyā jaṭilogrā ca lomaśā // 103
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣudrapattrī</s> (small-leaved), <s>maṅgalyā</s> (auspicious), <s>jaṭilā</s> (matted), <s>ugrā</s> (fierce), and <s>lomaśā</s> (hairy). //103//
<s>Vacā</s> (sweet flag), [also called] <s>ugragandhā</s> (strong-smelling), is pungent, bitter, and hot; it induces vomiting and stimulates the digestive fire;
It destroys constipation, flatulence, and colic, and purifies feces and urine;
It removes <s>apasmāra</s> (epilepsy), phlegmatic insanity, possession by spirits, worms, and disorders of <s>vāta</s> (wind). //104//
The Persian <s>vacā</s> (<s>pārasīka vacā</s>), which is white, is called <s>haimavatī</s>;
<s>Haimavatī</s>, as described, especially destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind). //105//
<s>Sugandhā</s> (the fragrant variety), also [called] <s>ugragandhā</s>, especially removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and cough;
It improves the voice, is appetizing, and purifies the heart, throat, and mouth. //106//

body.translated_text: The thick-knotted variety (<s>sthūlagranthiḥ</s>) is fragrant but is said to have lesser qualities. //107//

children.translated_text: The overseas <s>vacā</s> (<s>dvīpāntara vacā</s>) is somewhat bitter, hot, and stimulates the digestive fire;
It destroys constipation, flatulence, and colic, and purifies feces and urine. //108//
It removes <s>vātavyādhi</s> (diseases of wind), epilepsy, insanity, and bodily pain,
And especially destroys <s>phiraṅga</s> (syphilis). //109//
<s>Havuṣā</s> [is also called] <s>vapuṣā</s>, <s>visrā</s> (fetid), and <s>parāśvatthaphalā</s>;
<s>Matsyagandhā</s> (fish-smelling), <s>plīhahantrī</s> (spleen-destroyer), <s>viṣaghnī</s> (poison-destroyer), and <s>dhvāṅkṣanāśinī</s>. //110//

children.text: havuṣā dīpanī tiktā mṛdūṣṇā tuvarā guruḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Havuṣā</s> stimulates digestion, is bitter, mildly hot, astringent, and heavy;
It removes <s>pitta</s> (bile), abdominal enlargement, wind, hemorrhoids, bowel diseases, abdominal tumors, and colic;
The other variety (<s>parā</s>) is also said to have the same qualities; there is a difference in appearance between the two. //111//
<s>Viḍaṅga</s> (embelia) is [used in both] masculine and neuter [gender]; it is a worm-destroyer and insect-killer;
[It is also called] <s>taṇḍulā</s>, <s>vella</s>, <s>amoghā</s> (unfailing), and <s>citrataṇḍulā</s> (spotted-grain). //112//

children.text: viḍaṅgaṃ kaṭu tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ vahnikaraṃ laghu /
children.translated_text: <s>Viḍaṅga</s> is pungent, sharp, hot, dry, fire-kindling, and light;
It removes colic, flatulence, abdominal enlargement, <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), worms, <s>vāta</s> (wind), and constipation. //113//

body.translated_text: <s>Tumburu</s> [is also called] <s>saurabha</s> (fragrant), <s>saura</s>, <s>vanaja</s> (forest-born), <s>sānuja</s>, and <s>andhaka</s>. //114//

children.translated_text: <s>Tumburu</s> is well-known as bitter, and is pungent even in its post-digestive taste;

children.text: rūkṣoṣṇaṃ dīpanaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ rucyaṃ laghu vidāhi ca // 115
children.translated_text: It is dry, hot, digestive, sharp, appetizing, light, and irritating. //115//
It destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), diseases of the eyes, ears, and lips, headache, heaviness, and worms;
It eliminates skin diseases, colic, loss of appetite, dyspnea, splenic disorders, and urinary difficulties. //116//
<s>Vaṃśarocanā</s> (bamboo manna) [is also called] <s>vāṃśī</s>, <s>tugākṣīrī</s>, <s>tugā</s>, and <s>śubhā</s> (auspicious);

children.text: tvakkṣīrī vaṃśajā śubhrā vaṃśakṣīrī ca vaiṇavī // 117
children.translated_text: <s>Tvakkṣīrī</s> (bark-milk), <s>vaṃśajā</s> (bamboo-born), <s>śubhrā</s> (bright), <s>vaṃśakṣīrī</s>, and <s>vaiṇavī</s> (of bamboo). //117//

children.text: vaṃśajā bṛṃhaṇī vṛṣyā balyā svādvī ca śītalā /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaṃśajā</s> (bamboo manna) is nourishing, aphrodisiac, strengthening, sweet, and cooling;
It removes thirst, cough, fever, dyspnea, consumption, <s>pitta</s> (bile), blood disorders, and jaundice;
It removes skin diseases, wounds, and anemia; it is astringent and alleviates <s>vāta</s> and urinary disorders. //118//

body.translated_text: <s>Samudraphena</s> (cuttlefish bone) [is also called] <s>phena</s> (foam), <s>ḍiṇḍīra</s>, and <s>abdhikapha</s> (ocean-phlegm). //119//

children.translated_text: <s>Samudraphena</s> (cuttlefish bone) is beneficial for the eyes, scraping, and cooling;
It is astringent, destroys poison and <s>pitta</s> (bile), removes ear diseases and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), and is laxative. //120//
<s>Jīvaka</s>, <s>Ṛṣabhaka</s>, the two <s>Medā</s>s, the two <s>Kākolī</s>s, and <s>Ṛddhi</s>-<s>Vṛddhi</s> —
<s>Aṣṭavarga</s> (the group of eight) consists of these eight substances, as stated by <s>Caraka</s> and others. //121//

children.text: aṣṭavargo himaḥ svādur bṛṃhaṇaḥ śukralo guruḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Aṣṭavarga</s> is cooling, sweet, nourishing, semen-promoting, and heavy;
It promotes the union of broken bones, and increases strength, vigor, and vitality;
It removes <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), blood disorders, thirst, burning sensation, fever, urinary disorders, and consumption. //122//
<s>Jīvaka</s> and <s>Ṛṣabhaka</s> are known to grow on Himalayan peaks;
Their tubers are like garlic bulbs, pithy, and with small leaves. //123//
<s>Jīvaka</s> has a brush-like shape, while <s>Ṛṣabhaka</s> resembles a bull's horn;
<s>Jīvaka</s> is sweet, [also called] <s>śṛṅga</s> (horn), <s>hrasvāṅga</s> (short-bodied), and <s>kūrcaśīrṣaka</s> (brush-headed). //124//

children.text: ṛṣabho vṛṣabho dhīro viṣāṇī drākṣa ityapi /
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛṣabha</s> [is also called] <s>vṛṣabha</s> (bull), <s>dhīra</s> (steadfast), <s>viṣāṇī</s> (horned), and <s>drākṣa</s>;
<s>Jīvaka</s> and <s>Ṛṣabhaka</s> are strengthening, cooling, and promote semen and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm). //125//

body.translated_text: They are sweet and remove <s>pitta</s> (bile), burning sensation, blood disorders, emaciation, <s>vāta</s> (wind), and consumption. //126//

children.translated_text: The tuber called <s>Mahāmedā</s> grows in the <s>Moraṅga</s> region and such places;
<s>Mahāmedā</s>, <s>khanīmedā</s> — thus it has been stated by the great sages. //127//
Its tuber is white, resembling fresh ginger, creeper-born, and very pale;
This is known as <s>Mahāmedā</s>; now the characteristics of <s>Medā</s> are described. //128//
The white tuber, which when cut oozes a fatty substance like <s>medas</s> (fat),
That should be known as <s>Medā</s> by those persons eager to investigate. //129//
[<s>Medā</s> is also called] <s>śalyaparṇī</s>, <s>maṇicchidrā</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>medobhavā</s>, and <s>adhvarā</s>;
<s>Mahāmedā</s> [is also called] <s>vasucchidrā</s>, <s>tridantī</s>, and <s>devatāmaṇi</s>. //130//
The pair of <s>Medā</s>s is heavy, sweet, aphrodisiac, and promotes breast-milk and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm);
It is nourishing, cooling, and removes <s>pitta</s> (bile), blood disorders, <s>vāta</s> (wind), and fever. //131//

body.translated_text: <s>Kṣīrakākolī</s> grows in the same regions where <s>Mahāmedā</s> is found. //132//

children.text: yatra syāt kṣīrakākolī kākolī atra jāyate /
children.translated_text: Where <s>Kṣīrakākolī</s> grows, <s>Kākolī</s> also grows there;
Its tuber resembles that of <s>pīvarī</s>, is milky, and has a pleasant fragrance. //133//
That is called <s>Kṣīrakākolī</s>; now the identifying characteristics of <s>Kākolī</s> are described:

children.text: yathā syāt kṣīrakākolī kākolyapi tathā bhavet // 134
children.translated_text: As is <s>Kṣīrakākolī</s>, so also is <s>Kākolī</s>. //134//

children.text: eṣā kiṃcid bhavet kṛṣṇā bhedo 'yam ubhayor api /
children.translated_text: This one is somewhat dark — that is the difference between the two;

children.text: kākolī vāyasolī ca vīrā kāyasthikā tathā // 135
children.translated_text: <s>Kākolī</s> [is also called] <s>vāyasolī</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, and <s>kāyasthikā</s>. //135//
The white one is <s>Kṣīrakākolī</s>, [also called] <s>vayaḥsthā</s> and <s>kṣīravallikā</s>;
It is called <s>kṣīriṇī</s>, <s>dhīrā</s>, <s>kṣīraśuklā</s>, and <s>payasvinī</s> (milky). //136//
The pair of <s>Kākolī</s>s is cooling, semen-promoting, sweet, and heavy;
It is nourishing and removes <s>vāta</s> (wind), burning sensation, blood disorders, <s>pitta</s> (bile), wasting, and fever. //137//
<s>Ṛddhi</s> and <s>Vṛddhi</s> are two tubers that grow on the <s>Kośala</s> mountain;
The tuber is covered with white hairs, creeper-born, and porous. //138//

children.text: sa eva ṛddhirvṛddhiśca bhedam apyetayor bruve /
children.translated_text: That itself is [both] <s>Ṛddhi</s> and <s>Vṛddhi</s>; I now describe the difference between them:
<s>Ṛddhi</s> has knots like cotton clusters and has a leftward-spiraling fruit. //139//
<s>Vṛddhi</s> is described by the great sages as having a rightward-spiraling fruit;

children.text: ṛddhir yogyaṃ siddhilakṣmyau vṛddher apyāhvayā ime // 140
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛddhi</s> [is also called] <s>yogyā</s>, <s>siddhi</s>, and <s>lakṣmī</s>; these are also names of <s>Vṛddhi</s>. //140//

children.text: ṛddhir balyā tridoṣaghnī śukralā madhurā guruḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛddhi</s> is strengthening, destroys the three <s>doṣa</s>s, promotes semen, is sweet, and heavy;
It bestows vitality and sovereignty, and destroys fainting, blood disorders, and <s>pitta</s> (bile). //141//

children.text: vṛddhir garbhapradā śītā bṛṃhaṇī madhurā smṛtā /
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛddhi</s> promotes conception, is cooling, nourishing, and sweet;
It is aphrodisiac, pacifies <s>pitta</s> (bile) and blood disorders, and removes injury-related cough and consumption. //142//
Since this <s>aṣṭavarga</s> is extremely rare even for kings,
Therefore, the physician should use a substitute of equal qualities;
The substitute should resemble the principal [substance]. //143//
In place of <s>Medā</s> and <s>Mahāmedā</s>, [use] the root of <s>Śatāvarī</s>;
In place of <s>Jīvaka</s> and <s>Ṛṣabhaka</s>, [use] the root of <s>Vidārī</s>;
In place of <s>Kākolī</s> and <s>Kṣīrakākolī</s>, [use] the root of <s>Aśvagandhā</s>;
In place of <s>Ṛddhi</s> and <s>Vṛddhi</s>, [use] the tuber of <s>Vārāhī</s>, which is equal in qualities. //144//
<s>Yaṣṭīmadhu</s> (licorice) [is also called] <s>yaṣṭī</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and <s>klītaka</s>;
Another [name is] <s>klītanaka</s>; in water it is called <s>madhūlikā</s>. //145//

children.text: yaṣṭī himā guruḥ svādvī cakṣuṣyā balavarṇakṛt /
children.translated_text: <s>Yaṣṭī</s> (licorice) is cooling, heavy, sweet, beneficial for the eyes, and promotes strength and complexion;
It is very unctuous, semen-promoting, good for hair, improves the voice, and removes <s>pitta</s> (bile), <s>vāta</s> (wind), and blood disorders;
It removes wounds, swelling, poison, vomiting, thirst, fatigue, and consumption. //146//

children.text: kāmpillaḥ karkaśaś candro raktāṅgo rocano 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Kāmpilla</s> [is also called] <s>karkaśa</s> (rough), <s>candra</s>, <s>raktāṅga</s> (red-bodied), and <s>rocana</s>;
<s>Kāmpilla</s> destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), <s>pitta</s> (bile), blood disorders, worms, abdominal tumors, enlargement, and wounds;
It is purgative, pungent, and hot, and removes urinary disorders, flatulence, poison, and stones. //147//
<s>Āragvadha</s> (purging cassia) [is also called] <s>rājavṛkṣa</s> (king of trees), <s>śamyāka</s>, and <s>caturaṅgula</s> (four-fingers);
<s>Ārevata</s>, <s>vyādhighāta</s> (disease-destroyer), <s>kṛtamāla</s>, and <s>suvarṇaka</s> (golden). //148//
<s>Karṇikāra</s>, <s>dīrghaphala</s> (long-fruited), <s>svarṇāṅga</s> (gold-bodied), and <s>svarṇabhūṣaṇa</s> (gold-adorned);
<s>Āragvadha</s> is heavy, sweet, cooling, and the best among purgatives. //149//
It removes fever, heart disease, <s>pitta</s> (bile), blood disorders, <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>udāvarta</s> (upward movement of gases), and colic;
Its fruit is purgative, appetizing, and removes skin diseases, <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm). //150//

children.text: jvare tu satataṃ pathyaṃ koṣṭhaśuddhikaraṃ param // 151
children.translated_text: It is always wholesome in fever and is supreme for purifying the bowels. //151//

children.text: kaṭvī tu kaṭukā tiktā kṛṣṇabhedā kaṭaṃbharā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṭvī</s> [is also called] <s>kaṭukā</s> (pungent), <s>tiktā</s> (bitter), <s>kṛṣṇabhedā</s>, and <s>kaṭaṃbharā</s>;
<s>Aśokā</s>, <s>matsyaśakalā</s>, <s>cakrāṅgī</s>, and <s>śakulādanī</s>. //152//
<s>Matsyapittā</s>, <s>kāṇḍaruhā</s>, <s>rohiṇī</s>, and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>;

children.text: kaṭvī tu kaṭukā pāke tiktā rūkṣā himā laghuḥ // 153
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṭvī</s> is pungent in its post-digestive effect, bitter, dry, cooling, and light. //153//
It is purgative, appetizing, and a cardiac tonic; it removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and fever;
It eliminates <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders), dyspnea, cough, blood disorders, burning sensation, skin diseases, and worms. //154//
<s>Kirātatikta</s> (chirata) [is also called] <s>kairāta</s>, <s>kaṭutikta</s>, and <s>kirātaka</s>. //155//
<s>Kāṇḍatikta</s> (stem-bitter), <s>anāryatikta</s>, <s>bhūnimba</s> (earth-neem), and <s>rāmasenaka</s>;
Another <s>kirātaka</s> from <s>Nepāla</s> (Nepal) is called <s>ardhatikta</s> (half-bitter) and is a fever-destroyer. //156//

children.text: kirātaḥ sārako rūkṣaḥ śītalas tiktako laghuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kirāta</s> (chirata) is laxative, dry, cooling, bitter, and light;
It removes <s>saṃnipāta</s> (combined <s>doṣa</s>) fever, dyspnea, <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), <s>pitta</s> (bile), blood disorders, and burning;
It destroys cough, swelling, thirst, skin diseases, fever, wounds, and worms. //157//
The seeds of <s>Kuṭaja</s> are described [as follows]: <s>yava</s> (barley-like), <s>indrayava</s>, and likewise

children.text: kaliṅgaṃ cāpi kāliṅgaṃ tathā bhadrayavā api // 158
children.translated_text: <s>Kaliṅga</s>, <s>kāliṅga</s>, and also <s>bhadrayava</s>. //158//
Sometimes the name of <s>Indra</s> alone designates it;
Its fruits are [called] <s>indrayava</s> as well as <s>bhadrayava</s>. //159//
<s>Indrayava</s> destroys the three <s>doṣa</s>s, is astringent, pungent, and cooling. //160//
It removes fever, diarrhea, bleeding hemorrhoids, vomiting, erysipelas, and skin diseases;
It stimulates digestion and destroys rectal polyps, blood disorders, <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), and colic. //161//
<s>Madana</s> [is also called] <s>chardana</s> (emetic), <s>piṇḍa</s>, <s>naṭa</s> (actor), and <s>piṇḍītaka</s>;
<s>Karahāṭa</s>, <s>maruvaka</s>, <s>śalyaka</s>, and <s>viṣapuṣpaka</s> (poison-flowered). //162//
<s>Madana</s> is sweet, bitter, hot in potency, scraping, and light;
It induces vomiting, cures abscesses, and destroys nasal catarrh and wounds;
It is dry and removes skin diseases, <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), flatulence, swelling, abdominal tumors, and wounds. //163//

children.text: rāsnā yuktarasā rasyā suvahā rasanā rasā /
children.translated_text: <s>Rāsnā</s> [is also called] <s>yuktarasā</s>, <s>rasyā</s>, <s>suvahā</s>, <s>rasanā</s>, and <s>rasā</s>;

children.text: elāparṇī ca surasā sugandhā śreyasī tathā // 164
children.translated_text: <s>Elāparṇī</s> (cardamom-leaved), <s>surasā</s>, <s>sugandhā</s> (fragrant), and <s>śreyasī</s> (excellent). //164//
<s>Rāsnā</s>, [also called] <s>apācinī</s>, is bitter, heavy, hot, and removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind). //165//
It removes swelling, dyspnea, wind-blood disorders, <s>vāta</s> colic, and abdominal enlargement;
It destroys cough, fever, poison, cold, <s>vāta</s> disorders, and leucoderma. //166//
<s>Nākulī</s> [is also called] <s>surasā</s>, <s>nāgasugandhā</s>, and <s>gandhanākulī</s> (fragrant mongoose-plant);
<s>Nakuleṣṭā</s> (favored by mongooses), <s>bhujaṅgākṣī</s> (snake-eyed), <s>sarpāṅgī</s> (serpent-bodied), and <s>viṣanāśinī</s> (poison-destroying). //167//
<s>Nākulī</s> is astringent, bitter, pungent, and hot; it destroys
Snake-bite, spider-bite, scorpion-sting, rat-bite poison, fever, worms, and wounds. //168//
<s>Mācikā</s> [is also called] <s>prasthikā</s>, <s>ambaṣṭhā</s>, <s>āmbālikā</s>, and <s>ambikā</s>;
<s>Mayūravidalā</s>, <s>keśī</s>, <s>sahasrā</s>, and <s>bālamūlikā</s>. //169//

children.text: mācikāmlā rase pāke kaṣāyā śītalā laghuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Mācikā</s> is sour in taste and post-digestive effect, astringent, cooling, and light;
It removes chronic diarrhea, <s>pitta</s> (bile), blood disorders, <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), and throat diseases. //170//
<s>Tejasvinī</s>, <s>tejavatī</s>, <s>tejohvā</s>, and <s>tejanī</s>;
<s>Tejasvinī</s> removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), dyspnea, cough, diseases of the mouth, and <s>vāta</s> (wind);
It is digestive, hot, pungent, bitter, and stimulates appetite and the digestive fire. //171//
<s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> [is also called] <s>kaṭabhī</s>, <s>jyotiṣkā</s>, and <s>kaṅgunī</s>;
<s>Pārāvatapadī</s> (pigeon-footed), <s>piṇyā</s>, a creeper known as <s>kakundanī</s>. //172//
<s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> is pungent, bitter, laxative, and removes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind);
It is very hot, emetic, sharp, and promotes the digestive fire, intellect, and memory. //173//
<s>Kuṣṭha</s> (costus) [is also called] <s>rogāhvaya</s> (disease-named), <s>vāpya</s>, <s>pāribhavya</s>, and <s>utpala</s>. //174//

children.text: kuṣṭhamuṣṇaṃ kaṭu svādu śukralaṃ tiktakaṃ laghu /
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṣṭha</s> (costus) is hot, pungent, sweet, semen-promoting, bitter, and light;
It destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind), blood disorders, erysipelas, cough, skin diseases, wind, and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm). //175//

children.text: uktaṃ puṣkaramūlaṃ tu pauṣkaraṃ puṣkaraṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣkaramūla</s> [is also called] <s>pauṣkara</s> and <s>puṣkara</s>;
<s>Padmapatra</s> (lotus-leaved) and <s>kāśmīra</s> — these are said to be varieties of <s>kuṣṭha</s>. //176//
<s>Pauṣkara</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, and destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), and fever;
It destroys swelling, loss of appetite, and dyspnea, and especially removes pain in the sides. //177//
<s>Kaṭuparṇī</s> [is also called] <s>haimavatī</s>, <s>hemakṣīrī</s>, and <s>himāvatī</s>;
<s>Hemāhvā</s> (gold-named) and <s>pītadugdhā</s> (yellow-milked) — its root is called <s>oka</s>. //178//
<s>Hemāhvā</s> is purgative, bitter, laxative, and causes nausea;
It removes worms, itching, poison, flatulence, <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), <s>pitta</s> (bile), blood disorders, and skin diseases. //179//
<s>Śṛṅgī</s> [is also called] <s>karkaṭaśṛṅgī</s> (crab-horned) and <s>kulīraviṣāṇikā</s> (crayfish-horned);

children.text: ajaśṛṅgī tu cakrā ca karkaṭākhyā ca kīrtitā // 180
children.translated_text: <s>Ajaśṛṅgī</s> (goat-horned), <s>cakrā</s>, and <s>karkaṭākhyā</s> (crab-named). //180//
<s>Śṛṅgī</s> is astringent, bitter, hot, and [removes] <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), <s>vāta</s> (wind), consumption, and fever;
It removes dyspnea, upward-moving wind, thirst, cough, hiccups, loss of appetite, and vomiting. //181//

children.text: kaṭphalaḥ somavalkaś ca kaiṭaryaḥ kumbhikāpi ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṭphala</s> (box myrtle) [is also called] <s>somavalka</s> (soma-barked), <s>kaiṭarya</s>, and <s>kumbhikā</s>;
<s>Śrīparṇikā</s>, <s>kumudikā</s>, <s>bhadrā</s>, and <s>bhadravatī</s>. //182//
<s>Kaṭphala</s> is astringent, bitter, pungent, and destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), and fever;
It destroys dyspnea, urinary disorders, hemorrhoids, cough, throat diseases, and loss of appetite. //183//
<s>Bhārgī</s> [is also called] <s>bhṛgubhavā</s> (born of <s>Bhṛgu</s>), <s>padmā</s>, <s>phañjī</s>, and <s>brāhmaṇayaṣṭikā</s> (brahmin's staff);
<s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, <s>aṅgāravallī</s> (ember-creeper), <s>kharaśāka</s>, and <s>hañjikā</s>. //184//

children.text: bhārgī rūkṣā kaṭustiktā rucyoṣṇā pācanī laghuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhārgī</s> is dry, pungent, bitter, appetizing, hot, digestive, and light;
It stimulates digestion, is astringent, and certainly destroys abdominal tumors and blood disorders;
It removes swelling, cough, <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), dyspnea, nasal catarrh, fever, and <s>vāta</s> (wind). //185//
<s>Pāṣāṇabheda</s> (stone-breaker) [is also called] <s>aśmaghna</s> (stone-destroyer), <s>giribhid</s> (mountain-splitter), and <s>bhinnayojinī</s>;
<s>Aśmabheda</s> (stone-breaker) is cooling, bitter, astringent, and purifies the bladder. //186//
It is purgative and destroys <s>doṣa</s>s, hemorrhoids, abdominal tumors, urinary difficulty, stones, and heart diseases;
It also removes uterine diseases, urinary disorders, splenic enlargement, colic, and wounds. //187//

children.text: dhātakī dhātupuṣpī ca tāmrapuṣpī ca kuñjarā /
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātakī</s> [is also known as] <s>Dhātupuṣpī</s>, <s>Tāmrapuṣpī</s>, and <s>Kuñjarā</s>,

children.text: subhikṣā bahupuṣpī ca vahnijvālā ca sā smṛtā // 188
children.translated_text: <s>Subhikṣā</s>, <s>Bahupuṣpī</s>, and <s>Vahnijvālā</s> — thus is she known. (188)
<s>Dhātakī</s> is pungent, cooling, softening, astringent, and light,
it alleviates thirst, diarrhea, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, poison, worms, and <s>visarpa</s> (erysipelas). (189)
<s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s> (Indian madder) [is also known as] <s>Vikasā</s>, <s>Jiṅgī</s>, <s>Samaṅgā</s>, and <s>Kālameṣikā</s>, (190)
<s>Maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, <s>Bhaṇḍīrī</s>, <s>Bhaṇḍī</s>, and also <s>Yojanavallī</s>,
<s>Rasāyanī</s>, <s>Aruṇā</s>, <s>Kālā</s>, <s>Raktāṅgī</s>, and <s>Raktayaṣṭikā</s>. (191)
<s>Bhaṇḍītakī</s>, <s>Gambhīrī</s>, <s>Mañjūṣā</s>, and <s>Vastrarañjinī</s> (cloth-dyer),
<s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s> is sweet, bitter, astringent, and improves voice and complexion. (192)
It is heavy and hot, and alleviates poison, <s>kapha</s>, swelling, and diseases of the uterus, eyes, and ears,
it destroys bloody diarrhea, <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), blood disorders, <s>visarpa</s> (erysipelas), wounds, and urinary disorders. (193)
<s>Kusumbha</s> (safflower) [is also known as] <s>Vahniśikha</s> (flame-crested) and <s>Vastrarañjaka</s> (cloth-dyer),
<s>Kusumbha</s> aggravates <s>vāta</s>, and alleviates dysuria, blood disorders, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>. (194)
<s>Lākṣā</s> (lac) [is also known as] <s>Palaṃkaṣā</s>, <s>Alakta</s>, <s>Yāva</s>, <s>Vṛkṣāmaya</s>, and <s>Jatu</s> (resin),

children.text: lākṣā varṇyā himā balyā snigdhā ca tuvarā laghuḥ // 195
children.translated_text: <s>Lākṣā</s> improves complexion, is cooling, strengthening, unctuous, astringent, and light. (195)
It is not hot, and destroys <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, hiccups, cough, and fever,
it removes wounds, chest injuries, <s>visarpa</s> (erysipelas), worms, and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases). (196)
<s>Alaktaka</s> (lac dye) has similar properties, and especially destroys blemishes. (197)
<s>Haridrā</s> (turmeric) [is also known as] <s>Kāñcanī</s>, <s>Pītā</s>, <s>Niśākhyā</s>, and <s>Varavarṇinī</s>,
<s>Kṛmighnī</s> (worm-destroyer), <s>Haladī</s>, <s>Yoṣitpriyā</s> (beloved of women), and <s>Haṭṭavilāsinī</s>. (198)
<s>Haridrā</s> is pungent, bitter, dry, hot, and alleviates <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>,
it improves complexion and removes skin diseases, urinary disorders, blood disorders, swelling, anemia, and wounds. (199)
A variety of <s>Dārvī</s> [is known as] <s>Āmragandhā</s> (mango-scented), <s>Surabhīdāru</s>, and <s>Dāru</s>,
<s>Karpūrā</s>, <s>Padmapattrā</s>, <s>Surīmat</s>, and <s>Suratārakā</s>. (200)

children.text: āmragandhir haridrā yā sā śītā vātalā matā /
children.translated_text: The <s>Haridrā</s> which is <s>Āmragandhī</s> (mango-scented) is considered cooling and <s>vāta</s>-aggravating,
it alleviates <s>pitta</s>, is sweet, bitter, and destroys all itching. (201)
The tuber of wild turmeric (<s>Araṇyahaladī</s>) destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), <s>vāta</s>, and blood disorders. (202)

children.text: dārvī dāruharidrā ca parjanyā parjanīti ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Dārvī</s> [is also known as] <s>Dāruharidrā</s> (tree turmeric), <s>Parjanyā</s>, and <s>Parjanī</s>,
<s>Kaṭaṃkaṭerī</s>, <s>Pītā</s>, and it is also called <s>Pacampacā</s>,
it is also called <s>Kālīyaka</s> and also <s>Kāleyaka</s>. (203)
<s>Pītadru</s>, <s>Haridra</s>, <s>Pītadāru</s>, and <s>Pītaka</s>,
<s>Dārvī</s> has properties similar to <s>Niśā</s> (turmeric), but additionally cures diseases of the eyes, ears, and mouth. (204)

children.text: dārvīkvāthasamaṃ kṣīraṃ pādaṃ paktvā yadā ghanam /
children.translated_text: When milk equal in quantity to a decoction of <s>Dārvī</s> is cooked down to one-fourth and becomes thick,
then it is called <s>Rasāñjana</s>, and it is supremely beneficial for the eyes. (205)
<s>Rasāñjana</s> [is also known as] <s>Tārkṣyaśaila</s>, <s>Rasagarbha</s>, and <s>Tārkṣyaja</s>,
<s>Rasāñjana</s> is pungent and alleviates <s>kapha</s>, poison, and eye disorders. (206)
It is hot, rejuvenative, bitter, excising, and removes wound impurities. (207)
<s>Avalguja</s> [is also known as] <s>Vākucī</s>, <s>Somarājī</s>, and <s>Suparṇikā</s>,
<s>Śaśilekhā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇaphalā</s>, <s>Somā</s>, and <s>Pūtiphalī</s>. (208)
<s>Somavallī</s>, <s>Kālameṣī</s>, and <s>Kuṣṭhaghnī</s> (skin disease destroyer) — thus it is proclaimed,
<s>Vākucī</s> is sweet, bitter, pungent in <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect), and rejuvenative. (209)
It relieves constipation, promotes appetite, is laxative, and alleviates <s>kapha</s>, blood disorders, and <s>pitta</s>,
it is dry, cardiotonic, and destroys asthma, <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), urinary disorders, fever, and worms. (210)
Its fruit aggravates <s>pitta</s>, is pungent, and removes <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>,
it is good for hair and skin, and destroys worms, asthma, cough, swelling, toxins, and anemia. (211)
<s>Cakramarda</s> [is also known as] <s>Prapunnāṭī</s>, <s>Dadrughna</s> (ringworm-destroyer), and <s>Meṣalocana</s>,
<s>Padmāṭa</s>, <s>Eḍagaja</s>, <s>Cakrī</s>, and <s>Puṃnāṭa</s>. (212)
<s>Cakramarda</s> is light, sweet, dry, and alleviates <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s>,
it is cardiotonic, cooling, and removes <s>kapha</s>, asthma, <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), ringworm, and worms. (213)
Its fruit, being hot, destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), itching, ringworm, poison, and <s>vāta</s>,
it is known to be pungent and to destroy abdominal tumors, cough, worms, and asthma. (214)

children.text: viṣā tv ativiṣā viśvā śṛṅgī prativiṣāruṇā /
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣā</s> [is also known as] <s>Ativiṣā</s>, <s>Viśvā</s>, <s>Śṛṅgī</s>, <s>Prativiṣā</s>, and <s>Aruṇā</s>,
<s>Śuklakandā</s>, <s>Upaviṣā</s>, <s>Bhaṅgurā</s>, and <s>Ghuṇavallabhā</s>. (215)

children.text: viṣā soṣṇā kaṭustiktā pācanī dīpanī haret /
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣā</s> (aconite) is slightly hot, pungent, bitter, digestive, and appetizing; it removes
<s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, diarrhea, toxins, poison, cough, vomiting, and worms. (216)
<s>Lodhra</s> [is also known as] <s>Tilva</s>, <s>Tirīṭa</s>, <s>Śāvara</s>, and <s>Gālava</s>. (217)
The second variety is <s>Paṭṭikālodhra</s> [also known as] <s>Kramuka</s> and <s>Sthūlavalkala</s> (thick-barked),
<s>Jīrṇapattra</s>, <s>Bṛhatpattra</s>, <s>Paṭṭī</s>, and <s>Lākṣāprasādana</s>. (218)
<s>Lodhra</s> is absorbent, light, cooling, beneficial for the eyes, and alleviates <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>,
it is astringent and removes bleeding disorders, blood diseases, fever, diarrhea, and swelling. (219)
<s>Laśuna</s> (garlic) [is also known as] <s>Rasona</s>, <s>Ugragandha</s> (strong-smelling), and <s>Mahauṣadha</s> (great medicine),
<s>Ariṣṭa</s>, <s>Mlecchakanda</s>, <s>Yavaneṣṭa</s>, and <s>Rasonaka</s>. (220)
When <s>Vainateya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) carried away the nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) from the greatest of gods,
then a drop fell from it, and that became <s>Rasona</s> (garlic) on earth. (221)

children.text: pañcabhiś ca rasair yukto rasenāmlena varjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is endowed with five <s>rasas</s> (tastes), being devoid of only the sour taste,
therefore it is called <s>Rasona</s> (without one taste) by those who know the properties of substances. (222)
In the roots, a certain taste — bitter — is present; in the leaves,

children.text: nāle kaṣāya uddiṣṭo nālāgre lavaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: in the stem it is declared to be astringent, and at the tip of the stem it is said to be salty,

children.text: bīje tu madhuraḥ prokto rasas tadguṇavedibhiḥ // 223
children.translated_text: and in the seed the taste is declared to be sweet by those who know its properties. (223)

children.text: rasono bṛṃhaṇo vṛṣyaḥ snigdhoṣṇaḥ pācanaḥ saraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Rasona</s> (garlic) is nourishing, aphrodisiac, unctuous, hot, digestive, and laxative,

children.text: rase pāke ca kaṭukastīkṣṇo madhurako mataḥ // 224
children.translated_text: it is pungent in taste and <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect), sharp, and considered sweet. (224)
It promotes the healing of fractures, is beneficial for the throat, heavy, and increases <s>pitta</s> and blood,
it promotes strength and complexion, benefits intellect, is good for the eyes, and is rejuvenative. (225)
It destroys heart disease, chronic fever, abdominal pain, constipation, abdominal tumors, loss of appetite, cough, and swelling,
as well as hemorrhoids, <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), digestive weakness, parasites, <s>vāta</s>, asthma, and <s>kapha</s>. (226)

children.text: madyaṃ māṃsaṃ tathāmlaṃ ca hitaṃ laśunasevinām /
children.translated_text: Wine, meat, and sour substances are beneficial for those who consume garlic,
exercise, exposure to sun, anger, excessive water, milk, and jaggery —
a person consuming garlic should avoid these continuously. (227)
<s>Palāṇḍu</s> (onion) [is also known as] <s>Yavaneṣṭa</s>, <s>Durgandha</s> (foul-smelling), and <s>Mukhadūṣaka</s> (mouth-spoiler),
<s>Palāṇḍu</s> should be known by the wise as similar in properties to garlic. (228)
It is sweet in <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect) and taste, not very hot, produces <s>kapha</s>, and does not greatly aggravate <s>pitta</s>,
it removes only <s>vāta</s>, promotes strength and vigor, and is heavy. (229)
<s>Bhallātaka</s> (marking nut) is referred to in all three genders; [it is also called] <s>Aruṣka</s>, <s>Aruṣkara</s>, and <s>Agnika</s>,
also <s>Agnimukhī</s>, <s>Bhallī</s>, <s>Vīravṛkṣa</s> (hero-tree), and <s>Śophakṛt</s> (swelling-producer). (230)
The ripe fruit of <s>Bhallātaka</s> is sweet in <s>vipāka</s> and taste, and light,

children.text: kaṣāyaṃ pācanaṃ snigdhaṃ tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ chedi bhedanam // 231
children.translated_text: astringent, digestive, unctuous, sharp, hot, excising, and purgative. (231)
It promotes intellect, kindles digestive fire, and destroys <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, wounds, and abdominal diseases,
<s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), hemorrhoids, <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption), abdominal tumors, swelling, flatulence, fever, and worms. (232)
Its marrow is sweet, aphrodisiac, nourishing, and alleviates <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>,
its stalk (<s>Āruṣkara</s>) is sweet, alleviates <s>pitta</s>, promotes hair growth, and kindles digestive fire. (233)
<s>Bhallātaka</s> is astringent, hot, promotes semen, is sweet, and light,
it destroys <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, abdominal diseases, flatulence, <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), hemorrhoids, and <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption) disorders,
and also abdominal tumors, fever, <s>śvitra</s> (leucoderma), digestive weakness, worms, and wounds. (234)
<s>Bhaṅgā</s> (cannabis) [is also known as] <s>Gañjā</s>, <s>Mātulānī</s>, <s>Mādinī</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, and <s>Jayā</s>. (235)

children.text: bhaṅgā kaphaharī tiktā grāhiṇī pācanī laghuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaṅgā</s> removes <s>kapha</s>, is bitter, absorbent, digestive, and light,
sharp, hot, aggravates <s>pitta</s>, and increases delusion, sluggishness, speech, and digestive fire. (236)
A variety of sesame, <s>Khasatila</s> (poppy), is also known as <s>Khākhasa</s>,
the pod derived from the <s>Khākhasa</s> fruit is cooling and light. (237)

children.text: grāhi tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ ca vātakṛt kaphakāsahṛt // 238
children.translated_text: It is absorbent, bitter, astringent, aggravates <s>vāta</s>, and removes <s>kapha</s> and cough. (238)
It dries up the bodily tissues, is dry, intoxicating, and increases speech,
it causes momentary delusion, promotes taste, and with regular use destroys virility. (239)
The milky sap of the poppy fruit is called <s>Āphūka</s> (opium) or <s>Mahiphenaka</s>,
<s>Āphūka</s> (opium) is desiccating, absorbent, destroys <s>kapha</s>, and aggravates <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>,
and it has properties mostly similar to the pod derived from the poppy fruit. (240)
The poppy seeds are also called <s>Khākhasatila</s>. (241)
Poppy seeds are strengthening, aphrodisiac, and very heavy,
they produce <s>kapha</s> and pacify <s>vāta</s>. (242)
<s>Saindhava</s> (rock salt) [is also known as] <s>Śītaśiva</s>, <s>Māṇimantha</s>, and <s>Sindhuja</s> (born of Sindh),

children.text: saindhavaṃ lavaṇaṃ svādu dīpanaṃ pācanaṃ laghu /
children.translated_text: <s>Saindhava</s> salt is sweet, appetizing, digestive, and light,

children.text: snigdhaṃ rucyaṃ himaṃ vṛṣyaṃ sūkṣmaṃ netryaṃ tridoṣahṛt // 243
children.translated_text: unctuous, palatable, cooling, aphrodisiac, subtle, good for the eyes, and alleviates all three <s>doṣas</s>. (243)
<s>Śākambharīya</s>, also called <s>Guḍākhya</s>, and likewise <s>Raumaka</s>, (244)

children.text: guḍākhyaṃ laghu vātaghnam atyuṣṇaṃ bhedi pittalam /
children.translated_text: <s>Guḍākhya</s> salt is light, alleviates <s>vāta</s>, very hot, purgative, and aggravates <s>pitta</s>,

children.text: tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ cāpi sūkṣmaṃ cābhiṣyandi kaṭupāki ca // 245
children.translated_text: it is sharp, hot, subtle, causes secretions, and pungent in <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect). (245)

children.text: sāmudraṃ yattu lavaṇam akṣībaṃ vaśiraṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: That which is sea salt (<s>Sāmudra</s>) [is also known as] <s>Akṣība</s> and <s>Vaśira</s>,
<s>Samudraja</s>, <s>Sāgaraja</s>, and <s>Lavaṇodadhisambhava</s> (born from the salt ocean). (246)

children.text: sāmudraṃ madhuraṃ pāke satiktaṃ madhuraṃ guru /
children.translated_text: Sea salt is sweet in <s>vipāka</s>, slightly bitter, sweet in taste, and heavy,
not very hot, appetizing, purgative, compatible with milk, and non-irritating,
it produces <s>kapha</s>, alleviates <s>vāta</s>, is sharp, not dry, and not excessively cooling. (247)

children.text: viḍaṃ pākaṃ ca kṛtakaṃ tathā drāviḍamāsuram /
children.translated_text: <s>Viḍa</s> salt [is also known as] <s>Pāka</s>, <s>Kṛtaka</s>, <s>Drāviḍa</s>, and <s>Āsura</s>,
<s>Viḍa</s> salt, containing alkali, promotes the movement of <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> both upward and downward,
meaning it moves <s>kapha</s> upward and <s>vāta</s> downward. (248)

children.text: dīpanaṃ laghu tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ rucyaṃ vyavāyi ca /
children.translated_text: It is appetizing, light, sharp, hot, dry, palatable, and pervading,
it alleviates constipation, flatulence, distension, heart disease, heaviness, and pain. (249)

children.text: sauvarcalaṃ syād rucakaṃ manthapākaṃ ca tanmatam /
children.translated_text: <s>Sauvarcala</s> (black salt) [is also known as] <s>Rucaka</s> and <s>Manthapāka</s> — thus it is regarded,

children.text: rucakaṃ rocanaṃ bhedi dīpanaṃ pācanaṃ param // 250
children.translated_text: <s>Rucaka</s> promotes relish, is purgative, appetizing, and an excellent digestive. (250)
It is very unctuous, alleviates <s>vāta</s>, does not greatly aggravate <s>pitta</s>, is clear, and light,
it purifies eructation, is subtle, and conquers constipation, flatulence, and pain. (251)
<s>Audbhida</s> (terrestrial salt), the <s>Pāṃśulavaṇa</s> (earth salt), is that which arises from the earth itself,

children.text: kṣāraṃ guru kaṭu snigdhaṃ śītalaṃ vātanāśanam // 252
children.translated_text: it is alkaline, heavy, pungent, unctuous, cooling, and destroys <s>vāta</s>. (252)
<s>Caṇakāmlaka</s> (citric salt) is very hot, appetizing, and causes dental sensitivity,
it has a salty aftertaste, promotes appetite, and removes pain, indigestion, and constipation. (253)
<s>Pākya</s> alkali [is also known as] <s>Yavakṣāra</s> (barley alkali), <s>Yāvaśūka</s>, and <s>Yavāgraja</s>,
<s>Svarjikā</s> is also known as an alkali, [also called] <s>Kāpota</s> and <s>Sukhavarcaka</s>. (254)
A variety of <s>Svarjikā</s> is called <s>Suvarcikā</s> by those with specialized knowledge,
<s>Yavakṣāra</s> (barley alkali) is light, unctuous, very subtle, and kindles digestive fire. (255)
It destroys pain, <s>vāta</s>, toxins, <s>kapha</s>, asthma, and throat diseases,
anemia, hemorrhoids, <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption), abdominal tumors, flatulence, splenic diseases, and heart diseases. (256)
<s>Svarjikā</s> has fewer properties than that, and should be known as removing abdominal tumors and pain,
<s>Suvarcikā</s> should be understood by people as similar in properties to <s>Svarjikā</s>. (257)
<s>Saubhāgya</s> (borax), <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, an alkali, is called <s>Dhātudrāvaka</s> (metal flux),
<s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) kindles digestive fire, is dry, removes <s>kapha</s>, and aggravates <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>. (258)
<s>Svarjikā</s> and <s>Yāvaśūka</s> are described as the two alkalis,
and combined with <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), they are called the three alkalis. (259)
When combined, they produce the stated properties, and especially are excellent in removing abdominal tumors,
the alkalis derived from <s>Palāśa</s>, <s>Vajrī</s>, <s>Śikhari</s>, <s>Ciñcā</s>, <s>Arka</s>, <s>Tila</s>, and <s>Nāla</s>, (260)
together with <s>Yavaja</s> and <s>Svarjikā</s>, are described as the eight alkalis,
these alkalis are equal to fire and greatly remove abdominal tumors and pain. (261)
<s>Cukra</s> (vinegar) [is also known as] <s>Sahasravedhi</s>, <s>Rasāmla</s>, and <s>Śukla</s>,
<s>Cukra</s> (vinegar) is very sour, hot, appetizing, and an excellent digestive. (262)
It removes pain, abdominal tumors, constipation, toxins, <s>vāta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>, and is laxative,
it alleviates vomiting, thirst, bad taste in the mouth, heart distress, and digestive weakness. (263)

body.translated_text: When the pairs of <s>Medā</s>, <s>Jīvaka</s>, <s>Kākolī</s>, and <s>Ṛddhi</s> are unavailable, one should substitute in order <s>vārī</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, and <s>vārāhī</s>;

children.translated_text: <s>Bhāvaprakāśa</s>, <s>Vargaprakaraṇa</s>, <s>Karpūrādivarga</s> (Section on Camphor and Other Substances)

children.text: puṃsi klībe ca karpūraḥ sitābhro himavālukaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Karpūra</s> (camphor), used in masculine and neuter gender, [is also known as] <s>Sitābhra</s> and <s>Himavāluka</s>,
<s>Ghanasāra</s>, <s>Candrasaṃjña</s>, and <s>Himanāmā</s> — thus it is known. (1)
<s>Karpūra</s> (camphor) is cooling, aphrodisiac, beneficial for the eyes, scraping, and light,
fragrant, sweet, bitter, and removes <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and poison. (2)
It destroys thirst, bad taste in the mouth, obesity, and foul odor,
<s>Karpūra</s> (camphor) is said to be of two kinds, distinguished as processed and unprocessed,
they say that unprocessed camphor is superior in properties to processed camphor. (3)
The camphor known as <s>Cīnāka</s> is said to cause depletion of <s>kapha</s>,
it removes <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), itching, and vomiting, and has a bitter taste. (4)
<s>Mṛganābhi</s> (musk) [is also known as] <s>Mṛgamada</s> and <s>Sahasrabhit</s>,

children.text: kastūrikā ca kastūrī vedhamukhyā ca sā smṛtā // 5
children.translated_text: <s>Kastūrikā</s>, <s>Kastūrī</s>, and <s>Vedhamukhyā</s> — thus it is known. (5)
That from <s>Kāmarūpa</s> is black, that from <s>Nepāla</s> has a blue hue,
and that from <s>Kāśmīra</s> is tawny — thus <s>Kastūrī</s> (musk) is known to be of three varieties. (6)
That from <s>Kāmarūpa</s> is the best, that from <s>Nepāla</s> is middling,
and <s>Kastūrī</s> (musk) born in the land of <s>Kāśmīra</s> is considered the lowest. (7)

children.text: kastūrikā kaṭus tiktā kṣāroṣṇā śukralā guruḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kastūrikā</s> (musk) is pungent, bitter, alkaline, hot, promotes semen, and is heavy,
it removes <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, poison, vomiting, cold, foul odor, and consumption. (8)

children.text: latā kastūrikā tiktā svādvī vṛṣyā himā laghuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Latā Kastūrikā</s> (plant musk) is bitter, sweet, aphrodisiac, cooling, and light,
it is beneficial for the eyes, excising, and removes <s>kapha</s>, thirst, bladder diseases, and oral diseases. (9)
The potency of <s>Gandhamārjāra</s> (civet) is vigor-promoting and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>,
it removes itching and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), is good for the eyes, fragrant, and destroys body odor from sweat. (10)
<s>Śrīkhaṇḍa</s> and <s>Candana</s> (sandalwood), not feminine in gender, [are also known as] <s>Bhadraśrī</s> and <s>Tailaparṇika</s>,
<s>Gandhasāra</s> (essence of fragrance), <s>Malayaja</s> (born of the Malaya mountains), and <s>Candradyuti</s>. (11)

children.text: svāde tiktaṃ kaṣe pītaṃ chede raktaṃ tanau sitam /
children.translated_text: When tasted it is bitter, when rubbed it is yellow, when cut it is red, and on the body it appears white,
sandalwood with knots and hollows is said to be the best. (12)

children.text: candanaṃ śītalaṃ rūkṣaṃ tiktam āhlādanaṃ laghu /
children.translated_text: <s>Candana</s> (sandalwood) is cooling, dry, bitter, delightful, and light,
it removes fatigue, consumption, poison, <s>kapha</s>, thirst, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, and burning sensation. (13)

body.translated_text: <s>Kālīyaka</s>, also [known as] <s>Kālīya</s>, is yellowish, [and is also called] <s>Haricandana</s>, (14)

children.translated_text: <s>Haripriya</s>, <s>Kālasāra</s>, and also <s>Kālānusāryaka</s>,
<s>Kālīyaka</s> has properties similar to red sandalwood and especially destroys blemishes. (15)
Red sandalwood (<s>Raktacandana</s>) [is also known as] <s>Raktāṅga</s> and <s>Kṣudracandana</s>,
<s>Tilaparṇa</s>, <s>Raktasāra</s>, and it is known as <s>Pravālaphala</s> (coral-fruited). (16)
Red sandalwood is cooling, heavy, sweet, and removes vomiting, thirst, blood disorders, and <s>pitta</s>,
it is bitter, beneficial for eye injuries, aphrodisiac, and removes fever, wounds, and poison. (17)

children.text: pataṃgaṃ raktasāraṃ ca suraṅgaṃ rañjanaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Pataṅga</s> (sappan wood) [is also known as] <s>Raktasāra</s>, <s>Suraṅga</s>, and <s>Rañjana</s>,
<s>Paṭṭarañjaka</s>, <s>Pattūra</s>, and <s>Kucandana</s>. (18)
<s>Pataṃga</s> (red sandalwood) is sweet, cooling, and removes <s>pitta</s>, <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), wounds, and blood disorders;
it should be understood as similar to <s>haricandana</s> (yellow sandalwood), and especially destroys burning sensation. (19)
All types of <s>candana</s> (sandalwood) are similar in taste and other properties;

children.text: gandhena tu viśeṣo'sti pūrvaḥ śreṣṭhatamo guṇaiḥ // 20
children.translated_text: the distinction is in fragrance, and the first-mentioned (white sandalwood) is the best in qualities. (20)

children.text: aguru pravaraṃ lohaṃ rājārhaṃ yogajaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Aguru</s> (agarwood) has the following varieties: <s>pravara</s> (finest), <s>loha</s>, <s>rājārha</s> (fit for kings), <s>yogaja</s>,
<s>vaṃśika</s>, <s>kṛmija</s> (worm-produced), and also <s>kṛmijagdha</s> (worm-eaten) known as <s>anāryaka</s>. (21)

children.text: agurūṣṇaṃ kaṭu tvacyaṃ tiktaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca pittalam /
children.translated_text: <s>Aguru</s> is hot, pungent, beneficial for the skin, bitter, sharp, and aggravates <s>pitta</s>;
it is light, destroys diseases of the ear and eyes, and removes cold, <s>vāta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>. (22)
The black variety (<s>kṛṣṇāguru</s>) is superior in qualities and sinks in water like iron;
the oil derived from <s>aguru</s> is considered equal to <s>kṛṣṇāguru</s> (black agarwood). (23)

children.text: devadāru smṛtaṃ dārubhadraṃ dārv indradāru ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Devadāru</s> (Himalayan cedar) is also known as <s>dārubhadra</s>, <s>dāru</s>, <s>indradāru</s>,
<s>mastadāru</s>, <s>drukilima</s>, <s>kilima</s>, and <s>surabhūruha</s>. (24)

children.text: devadāru laghu snigdhaṃ tiktoṣṇaṃ kaṭupāki ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Devadāru</s> is light, unctuous, bitter, hot, and pungent in post-digestive effect;
it overcomes constipation, flatulence, swelling, <s>āma</s> (undigested matter), drowsiness, hiccups, fever, and blood disorders;
and removes <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders), rhinitis, <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), cough, itching, and <s>vāta</s>. (25)
<s>Sarala</s> (pine) is also known as <s>pītavṛkṣa</s> and <s>surabhidāruka</s>;
<s>Sarala</s> is sweet, bitter, pungent in post-digestive effect, and light. (26)
It is unctuous, hot, and is said to cure diseases of the ear, throat, and eyes, and to ward off evil spirits;
it removes <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, perspiration, burning sensation, cough, fainting, and wounds. (27)
<s>Tagara</s> (Indian valerian) is also known as <s>kālānusārya</s>, <s>kuṭila</s>, <s>nahuṣa</s>, <s>nata</s>;
another variety is <s>piṇḍatagara</s>, also called <s>daṇḍahastī</s> and <s>barhiṇa</s>. (28)
Both types of <s>tagara</s> are hot, sweet, unctuous, and known to be light;
they remove poison, epilepsy, colic, eye diseases, and disorders of all three <s>doṣas</s>. (29)
<s>Padmaka</s> (wild Himalayan cherry) is also known as <s>padmagandhi</s> and <s>padmāhvaya</s>;

children.text: padmakaṃ tuvaraṃ tiktaṃ śītalaṃ vātalaṃ laghu // 30
children.translated_text: <s>Padmaka</s> is astringent, bitter, cooling, <s>vāta</s>-aggravating, and light. (30)
It removes <s>vīsarpa</s> (erysipelas), burning sensation, blisters, skin diseases, <s>śleṣma</s>, blood disorders, and <s>pitta</s>;
it stabilizes pregnancy, promotes appetite, and removes vomiting, wounds, and thirst. (31)

children.text: guggulur devadhūpaś ca jaṭāyuḥ kauśikaḥ puraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Guggulu</s> (bdellium) is also known as <s>devadhūpa</s>, <s>jaṭāyu</s>, <s>kauśika</s>, <s>pura</s>;
<s>kumbholūkhalaka</s> (neuter gender), <s>mahiṣākṣa</s>, and <s>palaṃkaṣa</s>. (32)
<s>Mahiṣākṣa</s>, <s>mahānīla</s>, <s>kumuda</s>, and <s>padma</s> —

children.text: hiraṇyaḥ pañcamo jñeyo gugguloḥ pañca jātayaḥ // 33
children.translated_text: and <s>hiraṇya</s> as the fifth — these are known as the five varieties of <s>guggulu</s>. (33)
The one colored like a bee or collyrium is known as <s>mahiṣākṣa</s>;
<s>mahānīla</s> is recognized by characteristics matching its name (deep blue). (34)
<s>Kumuda</s> resembles a water lily (pale), and <s>padma</s> resembles a ruby;
<s>hiraṇya</s> is golden-colored — thus the distinguishing marks of the five varieties are described. (35)
<s>Mahiṣākṣa</s> and <s>mahānīla</s> are both beneficial for elephants;
<s>kumuda</s> and <s>padma</s> are supremely health-giving for horses. (36)
The golden variety (<s>hiraṇya</s>) is especially praised for humans;
though some authorities also consider <s>mahiṣākṣa</s> suitable for humans in certain cases. (37)

children.text: guggulur viśadas tikto vīryoṣṇaḥ pittalaḥ saraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Guggulu</s> is clear, bitter, hot in potency, <s>pitta</s>-aggravating, and laxative;

children.text: kaṣāyaḥ kaṭukaḥ pāke kaṭū rūkṣo laghuḥ paraḥ // 38
children.translated_text: astringent, pungent in post-digestive effect, pungent, dry, light, and supreme. (38)
It promotes union of fractures, is aphrodisiac, subtle, beneficial for the voice, and a rejuvenative;
it is appetizing, slimy, strengthening, and destroys <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, wounds, and glandular swellings. (39)
It conquers obesity, <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders), stones, <s>vāta</s>, moisture, skin diseases, <s>āma</s> (toxins), and wind disorders;
and overcomes boils, tumors, swelling, hemorrhoids, scrofula, and worms. (40)
Due to its sweetness it pacifies <s>vāta</s>, due to its astringency it destroys <s>pitta</s>,
and due to its bitterness it conquers <s>kapha</s> — thus <s>guggulu</s> destroys all <s>doṣas</s>. (41)

body.text: sa navo bṛṃhaṇo vṛṣyaḥ purāṇas tv atilekhanaḥ // 42
body.translated_text: When fresh, it is nourishing and aphrodisiac; when old, it is excessively reducing. (42)

children.translated_text: Fresh <s>guggulu</s> is unctuous, golden in appearance, resembling a ripe <s>jambū</s> (rose-apple) fruit,
fragrant, and slimy — this is declared to be new <s>guggulu</s>. (43)
That which is dry, foul-smelling, and has lost its natural color

children.text: purāṇaḥ sa tu vijñeyo guggulur vīryavarjitaḥ // 44
children.translated_text: should be known as old <s>guggulu</s>, devoid of potency. (44)
One who desires the benefits of <s>guggulu</s> should properly avoid sour foods, sharp substances, indigestion, sexual intercourse, exertion, exposure to sun,
alcohol, and anger — these are the regimen for one taking <s>guggulu</s>. (45)
<s>Śrīvāsa</s> (pine resin) is also known as <s>saralasrāva</s>, <s>śrīveṣṭa</s>, and <s>vṛkṣadhūpaka</s>;
<s>Śrīvāsa</s> is sweet, bitter, unctuous, hot, astringent, and laxative. (46)
It aggravates <s>pitta</s> and removes diseases of <s>vāta</s>, head, eyes, voice, and <s>kapha</s>;
it wards off evil spirits and removes perspiration, foul odor, lice, itching, and wounds. (47)
<s>Rāla</s> (resin of Shorea robusta) is also known as <s>śālaniryāsa</s> and <s>sarjarasa</s>;
also called <s>devadhūpa</s>, <s>yakṣadhūpa</s>, and <s>sarvarasa</s>. (48)

children.text: rālo himo gurus tiktaḥ kaṣāyo grāhako haret /
children.translated_text: <s>Rāla</s> is cooling, heavy, bitter, astringent, and absorbent; it removes
<s>doṣas</s>, blood disorders, perspiration, <s>vīsarpa</s> (erysipelas), fever, wounds, and cracked feet;
and cures afflictions by evil spirits, fractures, burns, colic, and diarrhea. (49)

body.translated_text: <s>Kunduru</s> (frankincense) is also known as <s>mukunda</s>, <s>sugandha</s>, and <s>kunda</s>. (50)

children.translated_text: <s>Kunduru</s> is sweet, bitter, sharp, beneficial for the skin, and pungent; it removes
fever, perspiration, evil spirits, inauspiciousness, diseases of the mouth, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>. (51)
<s>Sihlaka</s> (benzoin/olibanum) is also called <s>turuṣka</s>, as it originates from the <s>Yavana</s> (Greek/foreign) lands;
it is also known as <s>kapitaila</s> and <s>kapināmaka</s>. (52)
<s>Sihlaka</s> is pungent, sweet, unctuous, hot, and promotes semen and complexion;
it is aphrodisiac, beneficial for the throat, and removes perspiration, skin diseases, fever, burning sensation, and evil spirits. (53)
<s>Jātīphala</s> (nutmeg) is also known as <s>jātikośa</s> and <s>mālatīphala</s>;

children.text: jātīphalaṃ rase tiktaṃ tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ rocanaṃ laghu /
children.translated_text: <s>Jātīphala</s> is bitter in taste, sharp, hot, appetizing, and light,
pungent, digestive-stimulating, absorbent, beneficial for the voice, and removes <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s>. (54)
It destroys bad taste in the mouth, foul odor of impurities, and discoloration;
and cures worms, cough, vomiting, dyspnea, consumption, rhinitis, and heart disease. (55)

body.translated_text: The bark (outer covering) of <s>jātīphala</s> is called <s>jātīpattrī</s> (mace) by the best physicians. (56)

children.translated_text: <s>Jātīpattrī</s> (mace) is light, sweet, pungent, hot, and promotes appetite and complexion;
it removes <s>kapha</s>, cough, vomiting, dyspnea, thirst, worms, and poison. (57)
<s>Lavaṅga</s> (clove) is also known as <s>devakusuma</s>, <s>śrīsaṃjña</s>, and <s>śrīprasūnaka</s>;

children.text: lavaṃgaṃ kaṭukaṃ tiktaṃ laghu netrahitaṃ himam // 58
children.translated_text: <s>Lavaṅga</s> is pungent, bitter, light, beneficial for the eyes, and cooling. (58)
It is appetizing, digestive, palatable, and destroys <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and blood disorders;
it quickly destroys thirst, vomiting, flatulence, and colic;

children.text: kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ ca hikkāṃ ca kṣayaṃ kṣapayati dhruvam // 59
children.translated_text: and certainly eliminates cough, dyspnea, hiccups, and consumption. (59)

body.text: elā sthūlā ca bahulā pṛthvīkā tripuṭāpi ca // 60
body.translated_text: <s>Elā sthūlā</s> (greater cardamom) is also known as <s>bahulā</s>, <s>pṛthvīkā</s>, and <s>tripuṭā</s>. (60)

children.text: bhadrailā bṛhadelā ca candrabālā ca niṣkuṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: Also called <s>bhadrailā</s>, <s>bṛhadelā</s>, <s>candrabālā</s>, and <s>niṣkuṭi</s>;
<s>sthūlailā</s> is pungent in post-digestive effect, stimulates digestive fire in taste, and is light. (61)
It is dry, hot, and removes <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, itching, dyspnea, and thirst;
and cures nausea, poison, diseases of the bladder, mouth, and head, vomiting, and cough. (62)
<s>Sūkṣmā elā</s> (lesser cardamom) is also known as <s>upakuñcikā</s>, <s>tutthā</s>, <s>koraṅgī</s>, <s>drāviḍī</s>, <s>truṭi</s>;
<s>sūkṣmā elā</s> removes <s>kapha</s>, dyspnea, cough, hemorrhoids, and dysuria;

children.text: rase tu kaṭukā śītā laghvī vātaharī matā // 63
