children.translated_text: it is pungent in taste, cooling, light, and considered to remove <s>vāta</s>. (63)

children.text: tvakpattraṃ ca varāṅgaṃ syad bhṛṅgaṃ cocaṃ tathotkaṭam /
children.translated_text: <s>Tvakpattra</s> (cinnamon leaf/cassia bark) is also known as <s>varāṅga</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>coca</s>, and <s>utkaṭa</s>;

children.text: tvacaṃ laghūṣṇaṃ kaṭukaṃ svādu tiktaṃ ca rūkṣakam // 64
children.translated_text: <s>tvak</s> (cinnamon bark) is light, hot, pungent, sweet, bitter, and dry. (64)
It aggravates <s>pitta</s>, destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, and removes itching, <s>āma</s> (toxins), and loss of appetite;
and cures diseases of the heart, bladder, <s>vāta</s>, hemorrhoids, worms, rhinitis, and is anti-aphrodisiac. (65)

body.translated_text: <s>Tvaksvādvī</s> (Chinese cinnamon / sweet bark) is also known as <s>tanutvak</s> and <s>dārusitā</s>. (66)

children.translated_text: <s>Dārusitā</s> is said to be sweet, bitter, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>;
it is fragrant, promotes semen, improves complexion, and removes dryness of the mouth and thirst. (67)

children.text: pattrakaṃ tamālapattraṃ ca tathā syāt pattranāmakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Pattraka</s> (bay leaf / <s>tamālapatra</s>) is also simply known as <s>patra</s>;

children.text: pattrakaṃ madhuraṃ kiṃcit tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ picchilaṃ laghu /
children.translated_text: <s>Pattraka</s> is slightly sweet, sharp, hot, slimy, and light;
it destroys <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, hemorrhoids, nausea, loss of appetite, and rhinitis. (68)
<s>Nāgapuṣpa</s> (Mesua ferrea) is also known as <s>nāga</s>, <s>kesara</s>, and <s>nāgakesara</s>;
also called <s>cāmpeya</s>, <s>nāgakiñjalka</s>, and <s>kāñcanāhvaya</s>. (69)

body.translated_text: <s>Nāgapuṣpa</s> is astringent, hot, dry, light, and purifies <s>āma</s> (toxins). (70)

children.translated_text: It destroys fever, itching, thirst, perspiration, vomiting, and nausea;
and removes foul odor, skin diseases, <s>vīsarpa</s> (erysipelas), <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and poison. (71)
<s>Trijātaka</s> (<s>trisugandhi</s>, the three aromatics) is composed of equal parts of <s>tvak</s> (cinnamon), <s>elā</s> (cardamom), and <s>pattraka</s> (bay leaf);
when combined with <s>nāgakesara</s>, it is called <s>cāturjātaka</s> (the four aromatics). (72)
Both of these are appetizing, dry, sharp, hot, and remove bad breath;
they are light, promote <s>pitta</s> and digestive fire, improve complexion, and remove <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, and poison. (73)

children.text: kuṅkumaṃ ghusṛṇaṃ raktaṃ kāśmīraṃ pītakaṃ varam /
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) is also known as <s>ghusṛṇa</s>, <s>rakta</s>, <s>kāśmīra</s>, <s>pītaka</s>, and <s>vara</s>;
also called <s>saṃkoca</s>, <s>piśuna</s>, <s>dhīra</s>, <s>vāhlīka</s>, and <s>śoṇitābhidha</s>. (74)
The <s>kuṅkuma</s> that is produced in the land of <s>Kāśmīra</s>
has fine filaments, is deep red, and lotus-scented — that is the best quality. (75)
The <s>kuṅkuma</s> produced in the <s>Vāhlīka</s> region is said to be pale;
it has the scent of <s>ketakī</s> (screwpine) and fine filaments — this is of medium quality. (76)
The Persian (<s>pārasīka</s>) <s>kuṅkuma</s> has a honey-like fragrance;
it is slightly pale in color and has thick filaments — this is of the lowest quality. (77)
<s>Kuṅkuma</s> is pungent, unctuous, and overcomes headache, wounds, and parasites;
it is bitter, anti-emetic, complexion-enhancing, and removes blemishes and all three <s>doṣas</s>. (78)

children.text: gorocanā tu maṅgalyā vandyā gaurī ca rocanā /
children.translated_text: <s>Gorocanā</s> (cow bezoar/gallstone pigment) is also known as <s>maṅgalyā</s>, <s>vandyā</s>, <s>gaurī</s>, and <s>rocanā</s>;
<s>Gorocanā</s> is cooling, bitter, complexion-enhancing, and bestows auspiciousness and radiance;
it removes poison, inauspiciousness, evil spirits, madness, miscarriage, wounds, and blood disorders. (79)

body.translated_text: <s>Nakha</s> (nail-shaped shell/operculum) is also known as <s>vyāghranakha</s>, <s>vyāghrāyudha</s>, and <s>cakrakāraka</s>. (80)

children.translated_text: In small quantity it is called <s>nakhī</s>, also known as <s>hanuhaṭṭavilāsinī</s>;
<s>nakhadravya</s> removes evil spirits, <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), <s>vāta</s>, blood disorders, fever, and skin diseases. (81)
It is light, hot, promotes semen, enhances complexion, is sweet, and removes wounds and poison;
it removes inauspiciousness and foul odor of the mouth, and is pungent in both post-digestive effect and taste. (82)
<s>Bāla</s> (Coleus vettiveroides) is also known as <s>hrīvera</s>, <s>barhiṣṭha</s>, <s>udīcya</s>, and <s>keśāmbu</s>;
<s>Bālaka</s> is cooling, dry, light, appetizing, and digestive;
it cures nausea, loss of appetite, <s>vīsarpa</s> (erysipelas), heart disease, <s>āma</s> (toxins), and diarrhea. (83)
<s>Vīraṇa</s> (vetiver grass) is also known as <s>vīrataru</s>, <s>vīra</s>, and <s>bahumūlaka</s>;
<s>Vīraṇa</s> is digestive, cooling, anti-emetic, light, and bitter. (84)
It is astringent, removes fever, overcomes delusion and intoxication, and destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>;
and removes thirst, blood disorders, poison, <s>vīsarpa</s> (erysipelas), dysuria, burning sensation, and wounds. (85)

children.text: vīraṇasya tu mūlaṃ syāduśīraṃ naladaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: The root of <s>vīraṇa</s> is called <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver root), also known as <s>nalada</s>;

children.text: amṛṇālaṃ ca sevyaṃ ca samagandhikam ityapi // 86
children.translated_text: also called <s>amṛṇāla</s>, <s>sevya</s>, and <s>samagandhika</s>. (86)

body.text: uśīraṃ pācanaṃ śītaṃ stambhanaṃ laghu tiktakam // 87
body.translated_text: <s>Uśīra</s> is digestive, cooling, astringent, light, and bitter. (87)

children.translated_text: It is sweet, removes fever, overcomes vomiting and intoxication, and destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>;
and removes thirst, blood disorders, poison, <s>vīsarpa</s> (erysipelas), burning sensation, dysuria, and wounds. (88)
<s>Jaṭāmāṃsī</s> (spikenard) is also known as <s>bhūtajaṭā</s>, <s>jaṭilā</s>, and <s>tapasvinī</s>;

children.text: māṃsī tiktā kaṣāyā ca medhyā kāntibalapradā /
children.translated_text: <s>Māṃsī</s> is bitter, astringent, intellect-promoting, and bestows radiance and strength;
it is sweet, cooling, and removes all three <s>doṣas</s>, blood disorders, burning sensation, <s>vīsarpa</s> (erysipelas), and skin diseases. (89)

body.translated_text: <s>Śaileya</s> (lichen/stone flower) is also known as <s>śilāpuṣpa</s>, <s>vṛddha</s>, and <s>kālānusāryaka</s>. (90)

children.translated_text: <s>Śaileya</s> is cooling, pleasing, removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, and is light;
it removes itching, skin diseases, urinary stones, burning sensation, poison, and rectal bleeding. (91)

children.text: mustakaṃ na striyāṃ mustaṃ triṣu vāridanāmakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Mustaka</s> (nut grass) — the form <s>mustaka</s> is not feminine; <s>musta</s> is used in all three genders — is also known as <s>vārida</s>;
also called <s>kuruvinda</s>, and another variety is <s>kroḍakaseruka</s>. (92)

children.text: bhadramustaṃ ca gundrā ca tathā nāgaramustakaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhadramusta</s>, <s>gundrā</s>, and <s>nāgaramustaka</s> are also names for its varieties;

children.text: mustaṃ kaṭu himaṃ grāhi tiktaṃ dīpanapācanam // 93
children.translated_text: <s>Musta</s> is pungent, cooling, absorbent, bitter, appetizing, and digestive. (93)
It is astringent and removes <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, thirst, fever, loss of appetite, and worms;
the <s>mustaka</s> that grows in marshy regions is considered the best;
and among those, the sages have declared <s>nāgaramustaka</s> to be the finest. (94)
<s>Karcūra</s> (zedoary) is also known as <s>vedhamukhya</s>, <s>drāviḍa</s>, <s>kalpaka</s>, and <s>śaṭī</s>;

children.text: karcūro dīpano rucyaḥ kaṭukastikta eva ca // 95
children.translated_text: <s>Karcūra</s> is appetizing, palatable, pungent, and bitter. (95)
It is fragrant, pungent in post-digestive effect, and removes skin diseases, hemorrhoids, wounds, and cough;
it is hot, light, and removes dyspnea, abdominal tumors, <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and worms. (96)

body.translated_text: <s>Murā</s> (a fragrant root) is also known as <s>gandhakuṭī</s>, <s>daityā</s>, <s>surabhi</s>, and <s>śālaparṇikā</s>. (97)

children.text: murā tiktā himā svādvī laghvī pittānilāpahā /
children.translated_text: <s>Murā</s> is bitter, cooling, sweet, light, and removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s>;
it destroys fever, blood disorders, evil spirits, demons, skin diseases, and cough. (98)
<s>Śaṭhī</s> (a variety of zedoary) is also known as <s>palāśī</s>, <s>ṣaḍgranthā</s>, <s>suvratā</s>, and <s>gandhamūlikā</s>;
also called <s>gāndhārikā</s>, <s>gandhavadhū</s>, <s>vadhū</s>, and <s>palāśikā</s>. (99)
<s>Gandhapalāśī</s> (another name for <s>śaṭhī</s>) is astringent, absorbent, and light;
it is bitter, sharp, pungent, slightly hot, and destroys oral impurities;
it removes swelling, cough, wounds, dyspnea, colic, leukoderma, and evil spirits. (100)

body.text: priyaṅguḥ phalinī kāntā latā ca mahilāhvayā // 101
body.translated_text: <s>Priyaṅgu</s> (Callicarpa macrophylla) is also known as <s>phalinī</s>, <s>kāntā</s>, <s>latā</s>, and <s>mahilāhvayā</s>. (101)

children.translated_text: Also called <s>gundrā</s>, <s>gandhaphalā</s>, <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>viṣvaksenā</s>, and <s>aṅganāpriyā</s>;
<s>Priyaṅgu</s> is cooling, bitter, astringent, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>. (102)
It removes excessive bleeding, foul odor, perspiration, burning sensation, and fever;
and destroys abdominal tumors, thirst, poison, and delusion — similarly does <s>gandhapriyaṅgukā</s>. (103)

children.text: tatphalaṃ madhu rūkṣaṃ kaṣāyaṃ śītalaṃ guru /
children.translated_text: Its fruit is sweet, dry, astringent, cooling, and heavy;
it causes constipation and flatulence, gives strength, is absorbent, and overcomes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>. (104)

children.text: reṇukā rājaputrī ca nandinī kapilā dvijā /
children.translated_text: <s>Reṇukā</s> (Vitex agnus-castus) is also known as <s>rājaputrī</s>, <s>nandinī</s>, <s>kapilā</s>, and <s>dvijā</s>;
also called <s>bhasmagandhā</s>, <s>pāṇḍuputrī</s>, <s>kauntī</s>, and <s>hareṇukā</s>. (105)

children.text: reṇukā kaṭukā pāke tiktānuṣṇā kaṭur laghuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Reṇukā</s> is pungent in post-digestive effect, bitter, slightly hot, pungent, and light;
it aggravates <s>pitta</s>, is appetizing, intellect-promoting, digestive, and abortifacient;
it also causes <s>balāsa</s> (phlegmatic cough) and <s>vāta</s>, yet removes thirst, itching, poison, and burning sensation. (106)

children.text: granthiparṇaṃ granthikaṃ ca kākapucchaṃ ca gucchakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Granthiparṇa</s> (a knotted-leaf plant) is also known as <s>granthika</s>, <s>kākapuccha</s>, and <s>gucchaka</s>;
also called <s>nīlapuṣpa</s>, <s>sugandha</s>, and <s>tailaparṇaka</s>. (107)
<s>Granthiparṇa</s> is bitter, sharp, pungent, hot, appetizing, and light;
it destroys <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, poison, dyspnea, itching, and foul odor. (108)
<s>Sthauṇeyaka</s> (Taxus baccata / a fragrant substance) is also known as <s>barhibarha</s>, <s>śukabarha</s>, and <s>kukkura</s>;
also called <s>śīrṇaromaśuka</s>, <s>śukapuṣpa</s>, and <s>śukacchada</s>. (109)

body.text: sthauṇeyakaṃ kaṭu svādu tiktaṃ snigdhaṃ tridoṣanut // 110
body.translated_text: <s>Sthauṇeyaka</s> is pungent, sweet, bitter, unctuous, and removes all three <s>doṣas</s>. (110)

children.translated_text: It promotes intellect and semen, is palatable, wards off evil spirits, and overcomes fever and parasites;
it destroys skin diseases, blood disorders, thirst, burning sensation, foul odor, moles, and dark spots. (111)
<s>Coraka</s> (Angelica glauca) is also known as <s>niśācara</s>, <s>dhanahara</s>, <s>kitava</s>, <s>gaṇahāsa</s>,

children.text: corakaḥ śaṅkitaś caṇḍo duṣpattraḥ kṣemako ripuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>coraka</s>, <s>śaṅkita</s>, <s>caṇḍa</s>, <s>duṣpattra</s>, <s>kṣemaka</s>, and <s>ripu</s>.

children.text: rocako madhurastikaḥ kaṭuḥ pāke kaṭur laghuḥ // 112
children.translated_text: <s>Rocaka</s> (digestive salt) is sweet and bitter, pungent in post-digestive effect, pungent and light // 112
It is sharp, cardiotonic, cooling, and destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), itching, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>;
[It destroys] evil spirits, ill-fortune, perspiration, fat, blood disorders, fever, bad odor, poison, and wounds // 113

children.text: tālīśam uktaṃ pattrāḍhyaṃ dhātrīpattraṃ ca tatsmṛtam /
children.translated_text: <s>Tālīśa</s> is also known as <s>Pattrāḍhya</s> (leaf-rich) and <s>Dhātrīpattra</s>;
<s>Tālīśa</s> is light, sharp, and hot; [it destroys] <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), <s>kāsa</s> (cough), <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>;
It destroys <s>aruci</s> (anorexia), <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>āma</s> (undigested toxins), <s>vahnimāndya</s> (digestive weakness), and <s>kṣaya</s> (wasting diseases) // 114

body.text: kaṅkolaṃ kolaṃ proktaṃ cātha kośaphalaṃ smṛtam // 115
body.translated_text: <s>Kaṅkola</s> is also known as <s>Kola</s> and <s>Kośaphala</s> // 115

children.text: kaṅkolaṃ laghu tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ tiktaṃ hṛdyaṃ rucipradam /
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṅkola</s> is light, sharp, hot, bitter, cardiotonic, and promotes appetite;
It destroys oral malodor, heart disease, <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> disorders, and blindness // 116
<s>Gandhakokilā</s> is unctuous, hot, destroys <s>kapha</s>, is bitter, and fragrant;
<s>Gandhamālatī</s> should be known as equal to <s>Gandhakokilā</s> // 117
<s>Lāmajjaka</s> is also known as <s>Sunāla</s>, <s>Amṛṇāla</s>, <s>Lava</s>, and <s>Laghu</s>;
Also known as <s>Iṣṭakāpathaka</s>, <s>Savya</s>, <s>Nalada</s>, and <s>Vidātaka</s> // 118
<s>Lāmajjaka</s> is cooling, bitter, light, and conquers the three <s>doṣas</s> and blood disorders;
It removes skin diseases, excessive perspiration, dysuria, burning sensation, <s>pitta</s>, and blood disorders // 119
<s>Elavāluka</s> is also known as <s>Aileya</s>, <s>Sugandhi</s> (fragrant), and <s>Harivāluka</s>;
Also known as <s>Ailavāluka</s>, <s>Elālu</s>, <s>Kapittha</s>, and <s>Pattra</s> // 120

children.text: elālu kaṭukaṃ pāke kaṣāyaṃ śītalaṃ laghu /
children.translated_text: <s>Elālu</s> is pungent in post-digestive effect, astringent, cooling, and light;
It destroys itching, wounds, vomiting, thirst, cough, anorexia, and heart pain;
[It destroys] phlegm, poison, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), urinary disorders, and worms // 121
<s>Kuṭannaṭa</s> is also known as <s>Dāsapura</s>, <s>Bāleya</s>, and <s>Paripelava</s>;
Also known as <s>Plava</s>, <s>Gopura</s>, <s>Gonarda</s>, and <s>Kaivartīmustaka</s> // 122

body.translated_text: Resembling <s>Mustā</s>, having a soft covering, parrot-colored, it is also known as <s>Vitunnaka</s> // 123

children.text: vitunnakaṃ himaṃ tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ kaṭu kāntidam /
children.translated_text: <s>Vitunnaka</s> is cooling, bitter, astringent, pungent, and bestows luster;
It removes <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, <s>visarpa</s> (erysipelas), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), itching, and poison // 124

children.text: spṛkkāsṛg brāhmaṇo devo marunmālā latā laghuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Spṛkkā</s> is also known as <s>Asṛk</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Deva</s>, <s>Marunmālā</s>, <s>Latā</s>, and <s>Laghu</s>;
Also known as <s>Samudrāntā</s>, <s>Vadhū</s>, <s>Koṭivarṣā</s>, and <s>Laṅkopikā</s> // 125

children.text: spṛkkā svādvī himā vṛṣyā tiktā nikhiladoṣanut /
children.translated_text: <s>Spṛkkā</s> is sweet, cooling, aphrodisiac, bitter, and removes all <s>doṣas</s>;
It destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), itching, poison, perspiration, burning sensation, ill-fortune, fever, and blood disorders // 126

children.text: parpaṭī rañjanī kṛṣṇā jatukā jananī janī /
children.translated_text: <s>Parpaṭī</s> is also known as <s>Rañjanī</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Jatukā</s>, <s>Jananī</s>, and <s>Janī</s>;
Also known as <s>Jatukṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Agnisaṃsparśā</s>, <s>Jatukṛt</s>, and <s>Cakravartinī</s> // 127
<s>Parpaṭī</s> is astringent, bitter, cooling, complexion-enhancing, and light;
It removes poison and wounds, and destroys itching, <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases) // 128
<s>Nalikā</s> is also known as <s>Vidrumalatā</s>, <s>Kapotacaraṇā</s>, and <s>Naṭī</s>;
Also known as <s>Dhamanī</s>, <s>Añjanakeśī</s>, <s>Nirmedhyā</s>, <s>Suṣirā</s>, and <s>Nalī</s> // 129
<s>Nalikā</s> is cooling, light, beneficial for the eyes, and destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>;
It removes dysuria, urinary stones, <s>vāta</s>, thirst, blood disorders, <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), itching, and fever // 130
<s>Prapauṇḍarīka</s> is also known as <s>Pauṇḍarya</s>, <s>Cakṣuṣya</s> (eye-beneficial), and <s>Pauṇḍarīyaka</s>;

children.text: pauṇḍaryaṃ madhuraṃ tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ śukralaṃ himam /
children.translated_text: <s>Pauṇḍarya</s> is sweet, bitter, astringent, semen-promoting, and cooling;
It is beneficial for the eyes, sweet in post-digestive effect, complexion-enhancing, and removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s> // 131
<s>Bhāvaprakāśa</s>, <s>Vargaprakaraṇa</s>, <s>Guḍūcyādivarga</s> (Chapter on <s>Guḍūcī</s> and related plants)
Now, <s>Laṅkeśvara</s> (lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>), the proud <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
Afflicted by desire, forcibly abducted <s>Sītā</s>, the wife of <s>Rāma</s> // 1
Then the mighty <s>Rāma</s>, [pursuing] that enemy who had stolen his wife,
Accompanied by the monkey army, slew him at the forefront of battle // 2
When that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, enemy of the gods, proud of his strength, was slain,
<s>Devarāja</s> (king of gods) <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> (the thousand-eyed <s>Indra</s>) was greatly pleased with <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) // 3

children.text: tatra ye vānarāḥ kecid rākṣasair nihatā raṇe /
children.translated_text: Those monkeys who had been slain by the <s>Rākṣasas</s> in battle,
<s>Indra</s> revived them by sprinkling them with showers of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) // 4
Then, in those places where, having fallen from the bodies of the monkeys,
Drops of <s>pīyūṣa</s> (nectar) fell, from those [places] <s>Guḍūcī</s> was born // 5
<s>Guḍūcī</s> is also known as <s>Madhuparṇī</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s>, and <s>Amṛtavallarī</s>;
Also known as <s>Chinnā</s>, <s>Chinnaruhā</s>, <s>Chinnodbhavā</s>, and <s>Vatsādanī</s> // 6

children.text: jīvantī tantrikā somā somavallī ca kuṇḍalī /
children.translated_text: Also known as <s>Jīvantī</s>, <s>Tantrikā</s>, <s>Somā</s>, <s>Somavallī</s>, and <s>Kuṇḍalī</s>;
Also known as <s>Cakralakṣaṇikā</s>, <s>Dhīrā</s>, <s>Viśalyā</s>, and <s>Rasāyanī</s> // 7
Also known as <s>Candrahāsā</s>, <s>Vayaḥsthā</s>, <s>Maṇḍalī</s>, and <s>Devanirmitā</s> (created by the gods);
<s>Guḍūcī</s> is pungent, bitter, sweet in post-digestive effect, and is a rejuvenative // 8
It is binding, astringent, hot in potency, light, strength-giving, and kindles the digestive fire;
[It destroys] the three <s>doṣas</s>, <s>āma</s> (toxins), thirst, burning sensation, <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders), cough, and <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia) // 9
It removes <s>kāmalā</s> (jaundice), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), <s>vāta</s>, blood disorders, fever, worms, and vomiting;
It destroys <s>prameha</s> (diabetes), dyspnea, cough, piles, dysuria, heart disease, and <s>vāta</s> // 10
<s>Tāmbūla</s> (betel) is also known as <s>Tāmbūlavallī</s>, <s>Tāmbūlī</s>, <s>Nāginī</s>, and <s>Nāgavallarī</s>;

children.text: tāmbūlaṃ viśadaṃ rucyaṃ tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ tuvaraṃ saram // 11
children.translated_text: <s>Tāmbūla</s> is clear, appetizing, sharp, hot, astringent, and laxative // 11

children.text: vaśyaṃ tiktaṃ kaṭu kṣāraṃ raktapittakaraṃ laghu /
children.translated_text: It is enchanting, bitter, pungent, alkaline, causes <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), and is light;
It is strengthening and removes <s>kapha</s>, oral malodor, impurities, <s>vāta</s>, and fatigue // 12
<s>Bilva</s> is also known as <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, <s>Śailūṣa</s>, <s>Mālūra</s>, and <s>Śrīphala</s>;
<s>Śrīphala</s> (<s>Bilva</s>) is astringent, bitter, absorbent, dry, and produces digestive fire and <s>pitta</s>;
It removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, is strengthening, light, hot, and digestive // 13
<s>Gāmbhārī</s> is also known as <s>Bhadraparṇī</s>, <s>Śrīparṇī</s>, and <s>Madhuparṇikā</s>;
Also known as <s>Kāśmīrī</s>, <s>Kāśmarī</s>, <s>Hīrā</s>, <s>Kāśmarya</s>, and <s>Pītarohiṇī</s> // 14
Also known as <s>Kṛṣṇavṛntā</s>, <s>Madhurasā</s>, and <s>Mahākusumikā</s>;

children.text: kāśmarī tuvarā tiktā vīryoṣṇā madhurā guruḥ // 15
children.translated_text: <s>Kāśmarī</s> is astringent, bitter, hot in potency, sweet, and heavy // 15
It is appetizing, digestive, intellect-promoting, purgative, and conquers vertigo and wasting;
It removes <s>doṣas</s>, thirst, <s>āma</s> (toxins), colic, piles, poison, burning sensation, and fever // 16

children.text: tatphalaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ vṛṣyaṃ guru keśyaṃ rasāyanam /
children.translated_text: Its fruit is nourishing, aphrodisiac, heavy, good for hair, and a rejuvenative;
It removes <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, thirst, blood disorders, wasting, and urinary obstruction // 17

children.text: svādu pāke himaṃ snigdhaṃ tuvarāmlaṃ viśuddhikṛt /
children.translated_text: It is sweet in post-digestive effect, cooling, unctuous, astringent-sour, and purifying;
It destroys burning sensation, thirst, <s>vāta</s>, <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), wounds, and wasting // 18
<s>Pāṭalī</s> is also known as <s>Pāṭalā</s>, <s>Amoghā</s>, <s>Madhudūtī</s>, and <s>Phaleruhā</s>;
Also known as <s>Kṛṣṇavṛntā</s>, <s>Kuberākṣī</s>, <s>Kālasthālī</s>, and <s>Alivallabhā</s> // 19
Also known as <s>Tāmrapuṣpī</s>; another variety is the white <s>Pāṭalā</s>;
[The white variety is known as] <s>Muṣkaka</s>, <s>Mokṣaka</s>, <s>Ghaṇṭāpāṭalī</s>, and <s>Kāṣṭhapāṭalā</s> // 20
<s>Pāṭalā</s> is astringent, bitter, not excessively hot, and removes the three <s>doṣas</s>;
It removes anorexia, dyspnea, swelling, blood disorders, vomiting, hiccup, and thirst // 21

children.text: puṣpaṃ kaṣāyaṃ madhuraṃ himaṃ hṛdyaṃ kaphāsranut /
children.translated_text: Its flower is astringent, sweet, cooling, cardiotonic, and removes <s>kapha</s> and blood disorders;
It removes <s>pitta</s> and diarrhea, is beneficial for the throat; its fruit removes hiccup, blood disorders, and <s>pitta</s> // 22

children.text: agnimantho jayaḥ sa syāc chrīparṇī gaṇikārikā /
children.translated_text: <s>Agnimantha</s> is also known as <s>Jaya</s>, <s>Śrīparṇī</s>, and <s>Gaṇikārikā</s>;
Also known as <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Jayantī</s>, <s>Tarkārī</s>, <s>Nādeyī</s>, and <s>Vaijayantikā</s> // 23
<s>Agnimantha</s> removes swelling, is hot in potency, and destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>;
It removes <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), is pungent, bitter, astringent, sweet, and kindles the digestive fire // 24
<s>Śyonāka</s> is also known as <s>Śoṣaṇa</s>, <s>Naṭa</s>, <s>Kaṭvaṅga</s>, and <s>Ṭuṇṭuka</s>;
Also known as <s>Maṇḍūkaparṇa</s>, <s>Pattrorṇa</s>, <s>Śukanāsa</s>, and <s>Kuṭannaṭa</s> // 25
Also known as <s>Dīrghavṛnta</s>, <s>Aralu</s>, <s>Pṛthuśimba</s>, and <s>Kaṭaṃbhara</s>;
<s>Śyonāka</s> is appetizing, pungent in post-digestive effect, astringent, and cooling;
It is absorbent, bitter, and destroys <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and cough // 26

body.translated_text: The young fruit of <s>Ṭuṇṭuka</s> (<s>Śyonāka</s>) is dry and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s> // 27

children.text: hṛdyaṃ kaṣāyaṃ madhuraṃ rocanaṃ laghu dīpanam /
children.translated_text: It is cardiotonic, astringent, sweet, appetizing, light, and stimulates digestion;
It destroys <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), piles, and worms; when mature, it is heavy and aggravates <s>vāta</s> // 28
<s>Śrīphala</s> (<s>Bilva</s>), <s>Sarvatobhadrā</s> (<s>Gāmbhārī</s>), <s>Pāṭalā</s>, <s>Gaṇikārikā</s> (<s>Agnimantha</s>),
And <s>Śyonāka</s> — with these five, the great <s>Pañcamūla</s> (pentad of roots) is formed // 29
The great <s>Pañcamūla</s> is bitter, astringent, and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>;
It is sweet, destroys dyspnea and cough, is hot, light, and kindles the digestive fire // 30

children.text: śāliparṇī sthirā saumyā triparṇī pīvarī guhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Śāliparṇī</s> is also known as <s>Sthirā</s>, <s>Saumyā</s>, <s>Triparṇī</s>, <s>Pīvarī</s>, and <s>Guhā</s>;
Also known as <s>Vidārigandhā</s>, <s>Dīrghāṅgī</s>, <s>Dīrghapattrā</s>, and <s>Aṃśumatī</s> // 31

body.translated_text: <s>Śāliparṇī</s> is heavy and conquers vomiting, fever, dyspnea, and diarrhea // 32

children.translated_text: It removes wasting and the three <s>doṣas</s>, is nourishing, fitting, and a rejuvenative;
It is bitter, removes poison, is sweet, and removes wounds, cough, and worms // 33
<s>Pṛśniparṇī</s> is also known as <s>Pṛthakparṇī</s>, <s>Citraparṇī</s>, and <s>Ahiparṇī</s>;
Also known as <s>Kroṣṭuvinnā</s>, <s>Siṃhapucchī</s>, <s>Kalaśī</s>, and <s>Dhāvanī</s> // 34
<s>Pṛśniparṇī</s> destroys the three <s>doṣas</s>, is aphrodisiac, hot, sweet, and laxative;
It destroys burning sensation, fever, dyspnea, bleeding, diarrhea, thirst, and vomiting // 35
<s>Bṛhatī</s> is also known as <s>Vārttākī</s>, <s>Kṣudrabhaṇṭākī</s>, <s>Mahatī</s>, and <s>Kulī</s>;
Also known as <s>Hiṅgulī</s>, <s>Rāṣṭrikā</s>, <s>Siṃhī</s>, <s>Mahoṣṭrī</s>, and <s>Duṣpradharṣiṇī</s> // 36
<s>Bṛhatī</s> is absorbent, cardiotonic, digestive, and destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>;
It is pungent, bitter, and destroys oral bad taste, impurities, and anorexia;
It is hot and conquers <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), fever, dyspnea, colic, cough, and digestive weakness // 37

children.text: kaṇṭakārī tu duḥsparśā kṣudrā vyāghrī nidigdhikā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṇṭakārī</s> is also known as <s>Duḥsparśā</s>, <s>Kṣudrā</s>, <s>Vyāghrī</s>, and <s>Nidigdhikā</s>;
Also known as <s>Kaṇṭālikā</s>, <s>Kaṇṭakinī</s>, <s>Dhāvanī</s>, and <s>Bṛhatī</s> // 38
[Another variety:] the white, small [<s>Kaṇṭakārī</s>], also known as <s>Candrahāsā</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>, and <s>Kṣetradūtikā</s>;
Also known as <s>Garbhadā</s> (bestowing offspring), <s>Candramā</s>, <s>Candrī</s>, <s>Candrapuṣpā</s>, and <s>Priyaṃkarī</s> // 39

body.text: kaṇṭakārī sarā tiktā kaṭukā dīpanī laghuḥ // 40
body.translated_text: <s>Kaṇṭakārī</s> is laxative, bitter, pungent, appetizing, and light // 40

children.translated_text: It is dry, hot, digestive, and [destroys] cough, dyspnea, fever, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>;
It destroys nasal congestion, side pain, worms, and heart diseases // 41

children.text: tayoḥ phalaṃ kaṭu rase pāke ca kaṭukaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: The fruit of both [varieties] is pungent in taste and pungent in post-digestive effect;
It purges semen, is purgative, bitter, produces <s>pitta</s> and digestive fire, and is light;
It destroys <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, itching, cough, excess fat, worms, and fever // 42

body.text: tadvat proktā sitā kṣudrā viśeṣād garbhakāriṇī // 43
body.translated_text: The white small [variety] is described similarly, and is especially conducive to conception // 43

children.translated_text: <s>Gokṣura</s> is also known as <s>Kṣuraka</s>, <s>Trikaṇṭa</s>, and <s>Svādukaṇṭaka</s>;
Also known as <s>Gokaṇṭaka</s>, <s>Gokṣuraka</s>, and <s>Vanaśṛṅgāṭa</s> // 44

children.text: palaṃkaṣā śvadaṃṣṭrā ca tathā syād ikṣugandhikā /
children.translated_text: Also known as <s>Palaṃkaṣā</s>, <s>Śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, and <s>Ikṣugandhikā</s>;
<s>Gokṣura</s> is cooling, sweet, strength-giving, and purifies the bladder // 45
It is sweet, appetizing, aphrodisiac, nourishing, and removes urinary stones;
It destroys <s>prameha</s> (diabetes), dyspnea, cough, piles, dysuria, heart disease, and <s>vāta</s> // 46
<s>Śāliparṇī</s>, <s>Pṛśniparṇī</s>, <s>Vārttākī</s> (<s>Bṛhatī</s>), <s>Kaṇṭakārikā</s>,
And <s>Gokṣura</s> — with these five, the lesser <s>Pañcamūla</s> (pentad of roots) is formed // 47
The lesser <s>Pañcamūla</s> is light, sweet, strengthening, and removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s>;
It is not excessively hot, is nourishing, absorbent, and removes fever, dyspnea, and urinary stones // 48
From both <s>Pañcamūlas</s>, <s>Daśamūla</s> (the ten roots) is described;
<s>Daśamūla</s> destroys the three <s>doṣas</s>, dyspnea, cough, and headache;
It removes drowsiness, swelling, fever, abdominal distension, side pain, and anorexia // 49
<s>Jīvantī</s> is also known as <s>Jīvanī</s>, <s>Jīvā</s>, <s>Jīvanīyā</s>, and <s>Madhusravā</s>;
Also known as <s>Maṅgalyanāmadheyā</s> (auspiciously named), <s>Śākaśreṣṭhā</s> (best among vegetables), and <s>Payasvinī</s> // 50
<s>Jīvantī</s> is cooling, sweet, unctuous, and removes the three <s>doṣas</s>;
It is a rejuvenative, strength-giving, beneficial for the eyes, astringent, and light // 51

body.translated_text: <s>Mudgaparṇī</s> is also known as <s>Kākaparṇī</s>, <s>Sūryaparṇī</s>, <s>Alpikā</s>, and <s>Sahā</s> // 52

children.text: kākamudgā ca sā proktā tathā mārjāragandhikā /
children.translated_text: It is also called <s>Kākamudgā</s> and <s>Mārjāragandhikā</s>;

children.text: mudgaparṇī himā rūkṣā tiktā svāduśca śukralā // 53
children.translated_text: <s>Mudgaparṇī</s> is cooling, dry, bitter, sweet, and semen-promoting // 53
It is beneficial for the eyes, destroys wounds and swelling, is astringent, and removes fever and burning sensation;
It removes the three <s>doṣas</s>, is light, and conquers <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption), piles, and diarrhea // 54
